For this systematic review and meta-analysis, conducted from November 27, 2018, to June 29, 2021, a systematic literature search was conducted in MEDLINE/Ovid, Embase/Ovid, and Scopus databases to identify English-language articles that were published from inception through October 2020.

Study selection

Observational studies that reported on DR and its changes in pregnant women with preexisting T1D and T2D.

Data extraction and synthesis

Two independent reviewers extracted relevant data from each included study. Data were pooled using a random-effects model with the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation. This study followed the Meta-analysis of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) reporting guidelines.

Main outcomes and measures

Prevalence of any DR, proliferative DR (PDR), and DR progression rates.

Results

A total of 18 observational studies involving 1464 pregnant women with T1D and 262 pregnant women with T2D were included in the analysis. The pooled prevalence of any DR and PDR in early pregnancy was 52.3 (95% CI, 41.9-62.6) and 6.1 (95% CI, 3.1-9.8) per 100 pregnancies, respectively. The pooled progression rate per 100 pregnancies for new DR development was 15.0 (95% CI, 9.9-20.8), worsened nonproliferative DR was 31.0 (95% CI, 23.2-39.2), progression from nonproliferative DR to PDR was 6.3 (95% CI, 3.3-10.0), and worsened PDR was 37.0 (95% CI, 21.2-54.0). DR progression rates per 100 pregnancies were similar between the T1D and T2D groups, except for the development of new DR (T1D groups: 15.8; 95% CI, 10.5-21.9; T2D groups: 9.0; 95% CI, 4.9-14.8). A global trend toward a lower DR progression rate was observed after the 1989 St Vincent Declaration.

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this systematic review and meta-analysis suggest that women with T1D and T2D had a similar risk of DR progression during pregnancy. Despite improvements in the management of diabetes and diabetes during pregnancy, DR prevalence and progression in pregnant women with diabetes remains higher than the nonpregnant population with diabetes, highlighting the need to improve DR management in pregnancy.

records.title: Suprachoroidal Drug Delivery for VEGF Suppression in Wet AMD and Other Diseases With Choroidal Neovascularization.

content.title: Suprachoroidal Drug Delivery for VEGF Suppression in Wet AMD and Other Diseases With Choroidal Neovascularization.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Choroidal neovascularization caused by age-related macular degeneration, among other diseases, causes significant visual impairment. Intravitreal therapeutics inhibiting vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling have shown excellent safety and efficacy in regressing choroidal neovascularization and improving vision. Current US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved treatments deliver these drugs into the vitreous cavity, even though choroidal neovascularization originates from aberrant signaling in the choroid.

Design

Systematic review.

Methods

A literature search was conducted across PubMed and Google Scholar from inception up to December 31, 2024, focusing on studies investigating suprachoroidal delivery of anti-VEGF therapy. Randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, and case-control studies were included, whereas case reports and review articles were excluded.

Results

A total of 15 peer-reviewed articles, 3 press releases, 6 conference abstracts and presentations, and 8 clinical trials were identified that were relevant to the topic of suprachoroidal delivery of anti-VEGF therapy.

Conclusions

The suprachoroidal space is a potential space between the sclera and the choroid, which has recently become a route of delivery in an FDA-approved treatment. Notably, suprachoroidal delivery results in higher choroidal drug concentrations than intravitreal delivery. Promising results thus far have been seen with suprachoroidal delivery of VEGF-targeting therapies in clinical and preclinical studies; however, future work is needed to more fully demonstrate safety and efficacy.

records.title: Risk of Subsequent Dementia or Alzheimer Disease Among Patients With Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Risk of Subsequent Dementia or Alzheimer Disease Among Patients With Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Alzheimer disease (AD), a common form of dementia, shares several clinical and pathologic features with age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Epidemiologic reports on the association of AMD with subsequent dementia or AD are inconsistent.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

The Meta-analysis of Observational Studies in Epidemiology reporting guidelines were applied. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used to evaluate the risk of bias in the included cohort studies that examined the association of AMD with subsequent dementia or AD. We estimated the pooled hazard ratios (HRs) of dementia or AD using random effects model meta-analysis and subgroup analysis on different follow-up periods, AMD subtype, gender, age, study design, and methods to ascertain dementia or AD.

Results

A total of 8 223 581 participants were included in 8 studies published during 2000-2021. The meta-analysis showed that AMD was significantly associated with subsequent dementia (pooled HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01-1.47) or AD (pooled HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.03-1.43). Our secondary analysis revealed that the association was more noticeable in dry AMD than wet AMD.

Conclusions

Patients with AMD have higher risks of developing dementia or AD, and therefore identifying related comorbidities and retinal biomarkers is much warranted for older adults with AMD in ophthalmologic practice.

records.title: Comparison of Femtosecond Laser Assistance and Manual Trephination in Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty in the Treatment of Keratoconus: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Comparison of Femtosecond Laser Assistance and Manual Trephination in Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty in the Treatment of Keratoconus: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of femtosecond laser-assisted deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty (F-DALK) with those of manual-trephination DALK (M-DALK) in treating keratoconus.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

Through November 2022, we comprehensively searched PubMed, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, and 4 Chinese databases. Studies that involved comparisons between F-DALK and M-DALK groups and that reported on relevant efficacy and/or safety parameters were included. Primary outcomes were uncorrected- and corrected-distance visual acuity and intraoperative complication rates. Secondary outcomes were spherical equivalent, topographic astigmatism, refractive cylinder, mean keratometry, endothelial cell density, suture removal time, and postoperative complication rates. These data were analyzed using Cochrane Review Manager software version 5.3.

Results

This meta-analysis included 9 nonrandomized controlled studies involving 1713 eyes. In eyes treated with F-DALK, corrected-distance visual acuity at 1 to 6 months (weighted mean difference = -0.07 [95% confidence interval {CI} -0.10 to -0.03]; I2 = 0%; P < .001) after surgery was better and intraoperative Descemet membrane perforation occurred less often (odds ratio = 0.53 [95% CI 0.31-0.92]; I2 = 6%; P = .02) than in eyes treated with M-DALK. No clinically significant differences in other outcomes were found among the groups.

Conclusions

Both F-DALK and M-DALK are safe and efficacious for patients with keratoconus. Compared with M-DALK, F-DALK can provide better early visual acuity and reduce the intraoperative perforation rate, and its likely improvements to long-term visual quality and endothelial cell preservation warrant further investigation. In addition, the 2 techniques seem to be comparable regarding refractive outcomes and other complications.

records.title: Current Practices, Evolving Techniques, and Immunologic Challenges in Living and Deceased Donor Limbal Stem Cell Transplantation.

content.title: Current Practices, Evolving Techniques, and Immunologic Challenges in Living and Deceased Donor Limbal Stem Cell Transplantation.
content.abstract: This review focuses on allogeneic sources for restoring the ocular surface using limbal stem cell transplantation. We outline the current practices, evolving techniques, and immunologic challenges in living-related and deceased donor limbal stem cell transplantation. The diagnosis and staging guidelines for limbal stem cell deficiency are reviewed. We also explore the currently available treatment approaches, including the Cincinnati protocol for donor/recipient selection criteria and systemic immunosuppression (SI) regimen. Utilization of panel reactive antibody, HLA typing, ABO typing, and donor specific antibodies are highlighted. The traditional techniques as well as more novel variations are described. The importance of 3-agent SI protocols and patient adherence are emphasized to ensure excellent long-term outcomes. The primary immunologic challenge of allogeneic limbal stem cell transplantation, rejection, is also discussed in detail with recommended treatments, including a newer role for intravenous immunoglobulin. Other evolving practices have included a greater reliance on living-related conjunctival limbal allograft over deceased donor keratolimbal allograft due to improved outcomes, decreasing SI in older populations, and lengthening SI regimens due to the possibility of late acute rejection. Finally, we discuss the future of restoring the ocular surface via cell-based therapies, which may have the potential to decrease rejection.

records.title: International consensuses and controversies on causes, diagnosis and management of diabetic macular edema (DME).
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: International consensuses and controversies on causes, diagnosis and management of diabetic macular edema (DME).
content.abstract: Diabetic macular edema (DME) is the most common cause of vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy (VTDR) with an increasing prevalence tied to the global epidemic in diabetes. Despite significant advances, the management of DME remains a dynamic field with many unresolved controversies. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) allows objective assessment, however, correlation between vision and morphological changes can be inconsistent, causing disagreements on treatment strategies. DME is a complex disease with multifactorial pathophysiological pathways, leading to heterogenous treatment responses. There is a lack of standardized definition of treatment "non-response" and protocol for switching to second-line or adjuvant treatments. New anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) drugs and multi-targeted therapies seem to demonstrate improved durability, but long-term data is not yet available. Research in artificial intelligence (AI) is developing rapidly, however, rigorous appraisal of its reliability and generalizability are necessary before its implementation. Significant vision loss from DME in pregnant women, young children and elderly patients with systemic comorbidities are challenging conundrums. An international panel of experts (IPE) comprising 36 experts from 16 countries formulated and voted on the consensus statements in 5 key areas: 1) Diagnostic controversies around classification and imaging; 2) Treatment controversies; 3) Management paradigm between protocol-based and individualized approaches; 4) Emerging controversies in novel therapeutics and AI application, and 5) Special considerations for specific patient populations. There is an imminent need for mutual agreement on the best-possible approach to DME management in order to promote the optimal patient outcomes and to identify specific issues that require prioritization of resources and research.

records.title: Clinical histopathology and pathogenesis of macular telangiectasia type 2.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Clinical histopathology and pathogenesis of macular telangiectasia type 2.
content.abstract: Macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) is a rare neurodegenerative retinal disease defined by a unique combination of reduced macular pigment, a characteristic angiographic pattern, and a localized clinical presentation. The condition typically affects the temporal perifovea and leads to progressive visual impairment. No definitive treatment exists. Current management is limited to intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) injections for end-stage neovascular complications and the recently approved Encelto implant (Neurotech Pharmaceuticals, Inc.), which delivers ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) for neuroprotection. To clarify the still enigmatic pathophysiology of MacTel, we conducted a comprehensive review of all human histopathology reports published in English through December 31, 2024. Findings were systematically evaluated with respect to tissue processing techniques, postmortem fixation times, disease stage at last recorded ophthalmologic evaluation, diagnostic certainty, inclusion of control specimens, and the anatomic origin of analyzed retinal sections. This approach aimed to identify histopathologic features most likely to represent core disease mechanisms. Each of the features identified as most likely to be pathophysiologically relevant was independently assessed for clinical and histopathologic specificity. These features were then further interpreted in the context of genetic, metabolic, and anatomic associations reported in the literature. Donor demographics, coexisting ocular conditions, and systemic comorbidities were also reviewed to support the development of an integrative hypothesis for MacTel pathogenesis. Drawing on this synthesis, we propose a histopathology-informed model of disease pathophysiology and outline a provisional timeline for the contribution of key factors to clinical expression. We also review current neuroprotective strategies and provide targeted recommendations for future therapeutic development and histopathologic research. The conceptual framework developed in this work -grounded in rigorous analysis of the most consistent and methodologically validated histopathologic findings, and interpretation of their mechanistic context- may serve as a model for deciphering rare retinal diseases and for generating focused, hypothesis-driven questions to guide future investigation.

records.title: Performance of AI in predicting response to anti-VEGF treatment in DME using OCT images: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Performance of AI in predicting response to anti-VEGF treatment in DME using OCT images: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract: PurposeTo evaluate the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-based models in predicting response to anti-VEGF treatment in DME through meta-analysis.MethodsA comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Google Scholar up to November 20, 2025. Studies that developed machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) models using pretreatment optical coherence tomography (OCT) images to predict anatomical and/or functional response were included. A bivariate random-effects model was applied to estimate pooled sensitivity, specificity, positive likelihood ratio (PLR), negative likelihood ratio (NLR), diagnostic odds ratio (DOR), and the area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve (SROC AUC).ResultsTen studies encompassing 1927 anti-VEGF-treated patients with DME were included. Five studies employed ML-based approaches, while the remaining five used DL-based methods. The pooled sensitivity, specificity, PLR, NLR, DOR, and AUC of AI-based models were 0.88 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.84-0.91), 0.82 (95% CI: 0.78-0.86), 5.00 (95% CI: 3.86-6.47), 0.14 (95% CI: 0.11-0.20), 34.50 (95% CI: 20.28-58.67), and 0.91 (95% CI: 0.89-0.94), respectively. Overall, ML-based models showed higher pooled diagnostic performance than DL-based models, with higher sensitivity (0.91 vs. 0.82), specificity (0.85 vs. 0.78), PLR (6.05 vs. 3.70), lower NLR (0.11 vs. 0.23), higher DOR (56.16 vs. 16.41), and greater AUC (0.94 vs. 0.87). Deek's funnel plot showed no obvious publication bias, and Fagan's nomograms indicated favorable clinical utility of the prediction models.ConclusionAI-based models derived from pretreatment OCT images demonstrate promising discriminative ability in predicting response to anti-VEGF therapy in DME.

records.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
records.publisher: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

content.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) using a novel deep learning-based approach, and to evaluate longitudinal changes following shunt surgery.

Methods

In this prospective study, 22 patients with iNPH and 22 age-matched healthy controls underwent peripapillary optical coherence tomography (OCT). A deep learning-based ResUNet model enabled choroidal segmentation and quantification of total choroidal area (TCA), stromal choroidal area (SCA), luminal choroidal area (LCA), and the choroidal vascularity index (CVI). Measurements were compared between groups and reassessed in iNPH patients after ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery.

Results

Forty-four eyes of 22 iNPH patients and 44 eyes of 22 controls were analyzed. iNPH eyes exhibited significantly greater mean SCA compared to controls (adjusted p < 0.05). On the other hand, CVI remained comparable between groups. Following a mean follow-up of approximately 12 months after shunt surgery, mean SCA showed significant reduction (adjusted p < 0.05), whereas CVI remained unchanged.

Conclusions

iNPH was associated with peripapillary choroidal changes, predominantly involving the stromal compartment. Deep learning-based OCT analysis may provide a noninvasive approach for quantifying peripapillary choroidal microstructure, although the clinical relevance of these findings remains to be established.

records.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.

content.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to elucidate the expanding role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the early diagnosis of corneal and ocular surface diseases. AI has the potential to enhance diagnostic precision, streamline clinical workflows, and facilitate disease detection before clinical manifestations become evident.

Methods

A narrative literature review was conducted to assess the impact of AI and machine learning in corneal disease preclinical diagnosis. A comprehensive search in PubMed was performed using key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "deep learning," "corneal diseases," and "early diagnosis." Eligible studies were those published in English over the last decade that focused on AI-driven diagnostic approaches and prognostic modeling. Case reports, nonoriginal studies, and those with minimal AI integration were excluded. Data extraction emphasized AI methodologies, imaging techniques, diagnostic performance metrics, and clinical relevance.

Results

AI-powered machine learning models analyze vast imaging datasets, detecting subclinical abnormalities imperceptible to conventional diagnostic methods. This capability is particularly significant in early keratoconus detection, dystrophies, infectious keratitis, conjunctival neoplasia, and other corneal pathologies such as dry eye or Steven-Johnson disease, where subtle morphological changes precede clinically apparent disease.

Conclusions

The integration of AI into corneal disease diagnostics and management could mark in the future a transformative shift in Ophthalmology, offering precision, efficiency, and scalability. By facilitating early disease detection and individualized patient assessments, AI minimizes diagnostic inconsistencies and accelerates clinical decision making. Continuous algorithm refinement and real-world validation are crucial to maximizing AI's clinical utility. To fully harness AI's potential, multidisciplinary collaboration among ophthalmologists, data scientists, and regulatory bodies is imperative to address standardization, ethical concerns, and implementation barriers. As AI-driven technologies continue to evolve, they will redefine the standard of care in corneal disease diagnosis, therapeutic precision, and patient outcomes.

records.title: Automating systematic reviews in ophthalmology with the use of large language model deep research tools.

content.title: Automating systematic reviews in ophthalmology with the use of large language model deep research tools.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the performance of large language model (LLM) 'Deep Research' agentic systems for writing systematic reviews (SRs) in ophthalmology.

Methods

Structured prompts were submitted in September 2026 to Deep Research tools powered by GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 to produce SRs on the topics of 50 human-authored SRs published between May and August 2026 in ophthalmology journals (2025 Journal Impact Factor ≥ 3). Main outcomes included literature coverage (recall and precision against the studies included in the human-made SRs on the same topics), data extraction accuracy (discrepant numerical findings against cited sources), percentage of valid references and PRISMA adherence.

Results

One hundred SRs were produced, 50 for each LLM. Both LLMs showed limited overlap with the human-made SRs, with similar recall (38.0% vs. 38.3%; p = 0.859) and higher precision for GPT-6 Astra (53.2% vs. 36.8%; p < 0.001). GPT-6 Astra achieved a lower data reporting error rate (0.2%) compared to Claude Fable 5.1 (0.9%) (p < 0.001). The percentage of valid references was lower for GPT-6 Astra (79.2% vs. 91.4%; p < 0.001). PRISMA adherence was suboptimal for both models (50.2% vs. 55.2% of items fulfilled; p < 0.001).

Conclusion

GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 showed low data reporting error rates in evidence synthesis; however, incomplete literature coverage, bibliography management issues and poor adherence to reporting guidelines mandate human oversight, especially in study selection and quality appraisal.

records.title: Comparative Accuracy of a Commercial Multimodal Large Language Model Versus Clinicians in Dental Age and Sex Estimation from Panoramic Radiographs: A Benchmark Study.

content.title: Comparative Accuracy of a Commercial Multimodal Large Language Model Versus Clinicians in Dental Age and Sex Estimation from Panoramic Radiographs: A Benchmark Study.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Routine dental imaging captures cumulative dentoalveolar and periodontal changes, offering a non-invasive window into both chronological aging and physiological senescence. While task-specific deep learning models have been widely explored in dental radiology, the zero-shot diagnostic performance of commercial Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in adult populations remains underinvestigated. The aim of this study was to benchmark the zero-shot diagnostic accuracy and repeatability of a commercial MLLM against human clinicians of varying experience levels in estimating adult dental age and biological sex from panoramic radiographs (OPGs), using documented chronological age and biological sex as the ground truth. Methods: From 216 initially screened records, this retrospective single-center study included 127 standardized, anonymized OPGs from patients (74 men, 53 women; mean chronological age 55.5 ± 15.8 years, range 18-90 years) treated at the Clinical Department of Cranio-Maxillofacial Surgery, Military Institute of Medicine-National Research Institute in Warsaw. Each radiograph was independently evaluated across three trials by Gemini 3.1 Pro (Google, Mountain View, CA, USA) and once by two clinicians-a maxillofacial specialist (>10 years of experience) and a resident (<3 years of experience)-all blinded to clinical metadata. Results: Gemini 3.1 Pro demonstrated excellent repeatability across the three trials (ICC(A,1) = 0.926, ICC(A,3) = 0.974; p = 0.156) and moderate agreement with chronological age (ICC(A,1) = 0.604), but systematically overestimated age by a mean of 6.23 years. Mean absolute error (MAE) ranged from 12.91 to 13.03 years across the AI trials. The specialist achieved a significantly lower MAE (10.39 years) than all AI assessments (adjusted p ≤ 0.003), whereas the resident (MAE = 11.19 years) did not differ significantly from the AI (adjusted p = 0.282). In biological sex classification the specialist (66.1%) significantly outperformed all three AI trials (41.7-49.6%), while the resident (62.2%) significantly outperformed the first two AI trials (41.7% and 43.3%), but did not differ significantly from the third trial (49.6%). Across all runs, the AI exhibited significant directional asymmetry (p < 0.001), frequently misclassifying male patients as female. Conclusions: While Gemini 3.1 Pro demonstrated high internal repeatability and age-estimation accuracy comparable to a junior resident, its wide limits of agreement, systematic age overestimation, and poor sex-classification accuracy preclude its autonomous use in clinical or forensic workflows. Future studies incorporating healthy control cohorts and validated clinical indices are required to determine whether the observed age overestimation reflects inherent algorithmic miscalibration or sensitivity to cumulative dentoalveolar pathology in hospitalized patients.

records.title: Diabetic retinopathy feature utilisation in 54 convolutional neural networks: A heatmap analysis.

content.title: Diabetic retinopathy feature utilisation in 54 convolutional neural networks: A heatmap analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate how artificial intelligence (AI) systems detect referable diabetic retinopathy (DR) from retinal photographs by analysing heatmap patterns and determining their overlap with DR features.

Methods

Fifty-four AI systems were developed using 27 backbone architectures, with each implemented as both binary-referable and multi-class grading models based on the International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy (ICDR) grading scale. Models were trained on DDR, BRSET and Kaggle datasets. After training, each model analysed 749 images with DR feature annotations, with Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradients, LIME and SHAP heatmaps generated and compared to pixel-level annotations of microaneurysms, haemorrhages, exudates, cotton wool spots, venous beading, intraretinal microvascular abnormalities and neovascularisation.

Results

All models achieved acceptable predictive performance (AUROC >0.8 for most architectures). Heatmap analysis revealed consistent attention to the central and temporal macular region. Exudates and cotton wool spots were highlighted most frequently by the heatmaps, with venous beading and neovascularisation at the disc showing poor overall coverage for binary referable classifiers. Models grading per the ICDR scale demonstrated higher coverage for all features. Substantial variability was observed between architectures, suggesting different feature detection capabilities. Interestingly, the heatmap analysis indicated that the models may be using different features to the ICDR grading scale definitions.

Conclusion

AI models do not uniformly correlate with all DR features when detecting referable DR, limiting their predictive performance in unusual presentations. Heatmap aggregation analysis provides a scalable method for analysing model behaviour, allowing strengths and weaknesses to be assessed. These findings may help improve clinicians' trust and acceptance of AI.

records.title: Advances in Multimodal Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for the Diagnosis and Management of Diabetic Retinopathy: From Biomarkers to Personalized Care.

content.title: Advances in Multimodal Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for the Diagnosis and Management of Diabetic Retinopathy: From Biomarkers to Personalized Care.
content.abstract: Background and Objectives: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision loss. Staging based on colour fundus photography captures only part of a disease that involves the whole neurovascular unit and the retinal periphery. This narrative review summarizes the structural (optical coherence tomography, OCT), vascular (OCT angiography and ultra-widefield imaging) and functional (microperimetry, electrophysiology) biomarkers of DR, grades the evidence supporting each of them, and examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is changing screening, prognostication and treatment selection. Materials and Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for publications from January 2000 to May 2026, giving priority to randomized trials, prospective multicentre cohorts, systematic reviews and externally validated algorithms. Results: Among imaging biomarkers, disorganization of the retinal inner layers, outer retinal integrity and ultra-widefield angiographic non-perfusion have the most consistent prognostic evidence, whereas OCT angiography metrics remain device-dependent. AI has progressed from research classifiers to autonomous systems with regulatory authorization in the United States and the European Union, to prospectively evaluated deployments in national programmes and low-resource settings, and to time-to-event progression models and foundation models. Image-based prediction improves discrimination over clinical risk factors by modest margins, and biomarker-guided treatment of diabetic macular oedema still rests largely on retrospective series. Cross-device standardization of quantitative metrics, representative datasets, prospective outcome trials and health-economic evidence remain the main gaps. Conclusions: Individualized screening intervals are the application closest to routine practice, whereas phenotype-driven therapy and precision monitoring remain promising but unproven.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in clinical care: A comprehensive survey of Various AI-integrated technology, current state and future potential in healthcare.
records.publisher: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

content.title: Artificial intelligence in clinical care: A comprehensive survey of Various AI-integrated technology, current state and future potential in healthcare.
content.abstract: BackgroundIn our research work an extensive survey we thoroughly explore how artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning and deep learning techniques, are changing healthcare with the goal of improving disease detection, diagnosis, and treatment. The paradigm changes from healthcare 4.0 to healthcare 5.0 is being driven by AI.ObjectiveThis work begins with the roadmap of various enabling technologies that important in medical fields.MethodsThe work established by a methodical literature review and bibliometric approach to investigate different promising technologies like artificial intelligence, deep learning, natural language processing, and traditional machine learning, and assesses their applications in healthcare.ResultsImportant discoveries show that how artificial intelligent greatly increases diagnostic precision and supports personalized medicine; yet, incorporating these technologies into clinical processes, presents difficulties, including concerns about data quality, privacy, and ethics.ConclusionSeveral examples of healthcare use cases to improved interpretability and sophisticated AI models are needed in the future in healthcare 5.0, Lastly, combined with regulatory frameworks to guarantee deployment in healthcare settings both safe and efficient in future research.

records.title: The Emerging Role and Integration of Artificial Intelligence Tools in Veterinary Education: A Narrative Review.
records.publisher: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

content.title: The Emerging Role and Integration of Artificial Intelligence Tools in Veterinary Education: A Narrative Review.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), a data-driven and algorithm-supported technological system, has rapidly expanded its role in transforming daily life and professional practice over the past decade. In this narrative review, the recent literature was examined to evaluate current and emerging applications of AI in veterinary education and practice. A previously reported PubMed-focused search and a broader literature compilation served different purposes. The historical screening counts cannot be fully reconstructed, and the synthesis was narrative rather than systematic. Veterinary schools in the United States and elsewhere have begun exploring and integrating AI into Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) curricula to support teaching, learning, and competency development. This review summarizes recent advances in the application of AI in veterinary education. In anatomy, AI-based visualization and interactive tools are being explored, although controlled evidence of improved learning outcomes remains limited. In digital pathology, AI-assisted image analysis can provide students with opportunities to develop skills in recognizing and interpreting pathological findings. In clinical settings, AI models have shown potential in selected imaging and clinical-classification tasks, but their educational effectiveness requires further evaluation. Despite these advances, the broader implementation of AI in veterinary education and practice faces important regulatory and ethical challenges, including concerns regarding data privacy, algorithmic bias, academic integrity, and the reliability of AI-generated information. Addressing these issues will require multidisciplinary collaboration, multicenter data integration, appropriate validation, and strong ethical governance. With these foundations in place, AI may serve as a supportive educational and clinical tool rather than a replacement for veterinary educators and professionals. In the future, appropriately validated AI tools may contribute to veterinary education and clinical training.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.

content.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Research on artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis and clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) is expanding, but integrated evidence on publication patterns, keyword trajectories, online search activity, and methodological characteristics remains limited.

Objective

To characterize AI-CDSS research by integrating bibliometric analysis, Google Trends comparison, and structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications.

Methods

Scholarly interest was assessed using bibliometric analysis of Web of Science records from 2016 through August 2026, including author-keyword co-occurrence, bibliographic coupling, and reference co-citation, whereas Google Trends was used to characterize online search activity. A structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications was conducted to examine applications, methodological characteristics, and reported limitations.

Results

We analyzed 19,809 included publications from 2016 through August 2026. Output rose approximately 21-fold, from 193 records in 2016 to 4,082 in 2025. Output was geographically concentrated within the included corpus, with a Gini coefficient of 0.869. Among records with identifiable corresponding-author country or territory, China, the United States, and India accounted for 61.33%. Scientific Reports was the most frequent source (n = 916). Frequent artificial intelligence- and diagnosis-related keywords included machine learning (n = 5,666), deep learning (n = 4,022), and computer-aided diagnosis (n = 1,512). Bibliographic coupling identified 15 publication communities, and reference co-citation identified seven reference communities. In the monthly level-series comparison, 9 of 10 keyword concepts exhibited significant associations with Google Trends relative search interest, but none of the 10 first-difference associations remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Content analysis of 215 citation-ranked publications, including 191 empirical publications, showed frequent use of convolutional neural networks in diagnostic and radiology applications. Common limitations included limited external validation, infrequent calibration reporting, and sparse workflow-level or impact evaluation.

Conclusion

AI-CDSS research has rapidly expanded around machine learning, deep learning, and diagnostic applications, but the analyzed citation-ranked publications provide more evidence of methodological development than of clinical deployment. Integrating bibliometric, search-activity, and content-based perspectives shows limited short-term correspondence between online search activity and scholarly keyword use and highlights the need to move beyond model development toward independent external validation, prospective workflow and patient-outcome evaluation, calibration, fairness, and postdeployment monitoring.

records.title: More than a Second Pair of Eyes: Artificial Intelligence Across the Breast Imaging Pathway.

content.title: More than a Second Pair of Eyes: Artificial Intelligence Across the Breast Imaging Pathway.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from stand-alone accuracy studies to prospective deployment across breast screening, risk prediction, multimodal diagnosis, treatment response, and workflow support. The goal of this narrative review is to determine which AI applications have demonstrated clinical benefit, which remain technically promising, and what safeguards are required for implementation. We synthesize randomized trials, prospective cohorts, real-world implementations, external validations, systematic reviews, and guidance identified in PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus through 30 June 2026. In screening, AI-supported mammography can increase cancer detection and reduce reading workload, but effects depend on whether AI is used as concurrent support, an independent reader, triage, or partial autonomy; autonomous workflows may shift work and cost downstream through additional recalls. MASAI met its prespecified noninferiority criterion for interval cancer, but this should not be interpreted as proof of equivalence or mortality benefit. Image-based risk models often discriminate better than density or conventional clinical models, although prospective benefit from AI-guided allocation to supplemental imaging has not yet been demonstrated. Evidence for contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM), MRI, ultrasound, radiomics, and multimodal models is less mature and limited by external validation, domain shift, missing data, operator dependence, and uncertain incremental value beyond clinicopathological factors. Ungrounded large language models and opaque foundation models are not suitable for autonomous clinical advice. Current evidence therefore supports controlled, task-specific integration rather than radiologist replacement; real clinical benefit depends on governance of the whole AI-enabled pathway, including local validation, human factors, downstream resource use, statistical stopping rules, and fallback procedures.

records.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
records.publisher: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
content.abstract: Suicide is a leading, preventable cause of premature mortality, yet identifying individuals at imminent risk remains difficult. There are no validated biomarkers for routine stratification, and common approaches (clinical interviews, rating scales, self-report) are limited by subjectivity, reporting bias, and weak positive predictive value for rare outcomes. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-including machine learning, deep learning, and large language models-offer opportunities to integrate heterogeneous signals relevant to risk and treatment response. This narrative review summarizes recent AI-enabled prediction and characterization of suicidal thoughts and behaviors across major data modalities: structured electronic health records and claims; natural language processing of clinical notes and digital text; speech and facial/behavioral signals; neuroimaging and other neurobiological measures; and passive sensing from smartphones and wearables. We review common modeling and evaluation practices, emphasizing clinically relevant performance assessment (discrimination and calibration) and the importance of temporal and external validation. We also highlight barriers to translation, including class imbalance and label noise, dataset shift across sites and time, limited prospective evaluation, and the need for interpretable outputs that can support medication decisions and care pathways (e.g., triage, monitoring, and stepped interventions). Ethical and implementation challenges-privacy and consent, algorithmic bias and equity, governance, and the clinical consequences of false-positive and false-negative predictions-are discussed with an emphasis on safe deployment. We conclude with priorities for the field, including multimodal longitudinal cohorts, harmonized reporting standards, and pragmatic trials to determine whether AI decision support measurably improves suicide-prevention outcomes.

records.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.

content.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.
content.abstract:
Aim

Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents' clinical decision-making abilities.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction.

Results

The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001). Dimensional analysis showed that localization diagnosis, surgical method selection, risk identification, emergency response, and surgical timing judgment were higher in the experimental group than in the control group (all p < 0.05). The excellent rate for each assessment dimension (>85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.05). The satisfaction score was also higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice.
records.publisher: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

content.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) discourse in infectious disease (ID) has focused on benchmarking large language model chatbots against clinicians, a useful but narrowing inquiry. Agentic AI is a different paradigm: goal-directed systems that pursue clinical objectives over time, integrating data, invoking tools, monitoring results, and adapting without repeated prompting. This Viewpoint defines the anatomy of an agent, situates it within a 3-level framework (predictive, conversational, agentic), and examines how agents could transform 6 domains of ID practice: clinical care, antimicrobial stewardship, clinical microbiology, infection prevention and control, research, and epidemiology and pandemic preparedness. Individual components have proven value; integrated systems remain untested. No validated agentic system has been deployed in clinical ID; error propagation, algorithmic bias, cost, absent validation frameworks, undefined liability, and consequences for the workforce and its training must be addressed first. The ID community has a narrow window to shape these systems before decisions are made without it.

records.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.

content.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training.

Methods

A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study.

Results

On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681.

Discussion

These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

records.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.

content.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

Results

Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391).

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.

content.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.
content.abstract: The increasing complexity of tumor heterogeneity and variable therapeutic response has intensified the need for accurate personalized drug response prediction in oncology. Traditional trial-and-error chemotherapy strategies often result in suboptimal outcomes, toxicity, and delayed therapeutic adjustments. Rapid advances in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin modeling have significantly reshaped computational oncology research. This survey systematically reviews peer-reviewed research and review articles published from 2021 onward that investigate emerging computational paradigms integrating digital twins and multi-omics AI for drug response prediction. The foundational concepts in digital twin oncology, multi-omics profiling and AI-driven precision medicine are outlined initially. The existing approaches are categorized into four major paradigms such as omics-driven machine learning models, deep learning based multimodal architectures, mechanistic digital twin simulation frameworks and hybrid digital twin AI systems enabling adaptive therapy optimization. The multi-omics data integration strategies, including early, intermediate, late, network-based and graph/pathway-based fusion techniques. The survey synthesizes recent developments in drug sensitivity prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, tumor evolution forecasting and virtual clinical trials, while critically analyzing challenges related to data heterogeneity, interpretability, generalization, privacy, regulatory compliance and ethical considerations. Finally, future directions are highlighted such as real-time adaptive digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI and regulatory ready clinical deployment frameworks. Overall, this review provides a structured taxonomy, comparative analysis and research roadmap for advancing integrated digital twin and multi omics AI systems toward clinically actionable precision oncology.

records.title: Prevalence of hypothyroidism among pregnant women and associated feto-maternal outcomes in India: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: The Indian journal of medical research

content.title: Prevalence of hypothyroidism among pregnant women and associated feto-maternal outcomes in India: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract: Background and objectives Hypothyroidism is the most common thyroid disorder during pregnancy and, if not managed adequately, increases the risk of adverse foeto-maternal outcomes. The present systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to assess the prevalence of hypothyroidism among Indian pregnant women and related foeto-maternal outcomes. Methods A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Google Scholar, and preprint servers to identify observational studies reporting the prevalence of hypothyroidism and associated foeto-maternal outcomes among Indian pregnant women. A random-effects model was utilised to pool effect sizes, and heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistic. Funnel plots, along with Begg's and Egger's tests, were used to assess publication bias. Data were analysed using STATA version 17. Results A total of 60 studies were included. The pooled prevalence of hypothyroidism among pregnant women was 17% [95% confidence interval (CI): 14%, 19%] with subclinical hypothyroidism at 15% (95% CI: 12%, 18%) and overt hypothyroidism at 3% (95% CI: 3%, 4%). In women with subclinical hypothyroidism, the pooled prevalence of adverse maternal outcomes was 9% (95% CI: 6%, 11%), while the prevalence of adverse foetal outcomes was 11% (95% CI: 9%, 14%). The pooled prevalence was 18% for preterm birth (95% CI: 11%, 25%), 17% for low birth weight (95% CI: 10%, 25%), 7% for intrauterine death (95% CI: 2, 14%), and 2% for stillbirth (95% CI: 0, 4%). Among women with overt hypothyroidism, the prevalence of adverse maternal and foetal outcomes was 12% (95% CI: 10%, 15%) and 14% (95% CI: 11%, 17%), respectively. The pooled prevalence was 22% for low birth weight (95% CI: 13%, 31%), 16% for preterm birth (95% CI: 9%, 24%), 16% for intrauterine death (95% CI: 7%, 27%), and 6% for stillbirth (95% CI: 1%, 13%). Most studies used trimester-specific TSH cut-offs based on the American Thyroid Association guidelines. One fourth (n=15) of the 60 studies applied alternative thresholds, with upper limits for normal TSH varying from 4.0-10.0 mIU/L. Interpretation and conclusions The rising burden and adverse consequences of hypothyroidism in pregnancy demand urgent attention. Uniform, evidence-based screening and management practices must be implemented at all levels of care. There is a pressing need for India-specific diagnostic cut-offs and large-scale prospective studies to inform treatment thresholds and long-term outcomes.

records.title: Decoding neuronal gene expression: integrative insights from omics and AI.

content.title: Decoding neuronal gene expression: integrative insights from omics and AI.
content.abstract: Neuronal functional diversity and pathological vulnerability are governed by multi-layered regulatory programs. While high-throughput omics and neuroimaging provide high-resolution snapshots of these programs, bridging the gap between molecular dynamics and macro-scale brain architecture remains a significant informatics challenge. This review synthesizes the evolution of computational frameworks in neuro-omics-transitioning from descriptive co-expression modules to causal graph neural networks and cross-scale foundation models. We evaluate these methodologies within the context of Alzheimer's disease, schizophrenia, and epilepsy, identifying critical bottlenecks in data harmonization, spatial alignment, and causal interpretability.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Gastrointestinal Wireless Capsule Endoscopy: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Gastrointestinal Wireless Capsule Endoscopy: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract: Background: Wireless capsule endoscopy is widely used for diagnosing gastrointestinal diseases, but manual interpretation of capsule videos is time-consuming and can vary between clinicians. Artificial intelligence has been increasingly studied to support capsule analysis and reduce clinical workload. This systematic literature review and meta-analysis summarizes current evidence on artificial intelligence methods applied to wireless capsule endoscopy, with a focus on diagnostic performance, validation strategies, and clinical readiness. Methods: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Original journal articles were included based on predefined eligibility criteria. The reviewed studies addressed multiple artificial intelligence tasks, including detection, classification, segmentation, and localization of gastrointestinal abnormalities. Results: A total of 72 studies were included. Meta-analysis using random effects models showed high pooled diagnostic performance across clinical indications and gastrointestinal tract locations, with the strongest results reported for bleeding and vascular lesions and more variable performance for inflammatory bowel disease and mixed abnormality categories. The review also identified important clinical and technical barriers that may limit reliability and slow clinical adoption. These included limited external validation, small patient cohorts, retrospective study designs, and inconsistent reporting and evaluation practices. Conclusions: Artificial intelligence methods show strong potential to support wireless capsule endoscopy interpretation. Based on the findings, we propose practical recommendations to improve study design and validation. If these recommendations are applied, future studies may report more robust and reliable results, supporting better translation into clinical workflows.

records.title: AI-driven diagnostic and prognostic models for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: insights from clinical, imaging, and multi-omics studies-a scoping review.

content.title: AI-driven diagnostic and prognostic models for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: insights from clinical, imaging, and multi-omics studies-a scoping review.
content.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly known as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), is the most common chronic liver disease around the world, affecting 33.6% of the adult population (95% CI: 28.1%-39.5%; I 2 = 99.9%), or roughly one in three. The extent of the liver damage is variable, from simple steatosis to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH, formerly NASH), cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Early diagnosis is essential to prevent serious liver damage. Traditional diagnostic techniques such as liver biopsy, imaging, and biomarker testing are all invasive, costly, reduced sensitive to early-stage disease, and they also have variability among observers. Modern diagnostic and prognostic approaches based on the principles of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and specifically on machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have enabled multimodal approaches integrating clinical, imaging and molecular data. This scoping review conducted per PRISMA-ScR guidelines, synthesizes findings from 73 studies (search window 2020-2026) across three dimensions: clinical data driven models, imaging-based classifiers (ultrasound, CT and MRI), and multi-omics (genomics, transcriptomics and proteomics) techniques. Moreover, emergence of models such as U-Net and LiverNet 2.x, classification models like DeepLiverNet and BiLSTM models, as well as transformer frameworks and the identification of biomarkers models are also described. This study also investigates challenges such as data heterogeneity, data interpretability, fairness and real-world clinical application. Finally, important areas of research opportunities and future directions are highlighted to present a developing clinically applicable, explainable and ethical AI solutions to manage MASLD.

records.title: Exploring Translational Medical Research Progress in G20 Countries: <i>5-Year Study</i>.

content.title: Exploring Translational Medical Research Progress in G20 Countries: <i>5-Year Study</i>.
content.abstract:
Objectives

Biomedical research is crucial for advancing medical knowledge and improving public health. However, the research process is often disjointed and lacks seamless progression, leading to delays and missed opportunities. To address this, the concept of translational research has emerged, focusing on the smooth transition of research results to the next stage of inquiry.

Methods

This study analyzed approximately 40,000 research publications from the Web of Science database to identify research activities associated with translational research. Publications from Group of 20 (G20) countries over the past 5 years were examined to explore patterns of research focus and progress in this field.

Results

There is no universal formula for successful translational research across G20 countries. What works in one country may not yield the same results in another, as factors contributing to success vary significantly among nations. Each country's unique history of success and failure influences its translational research outcomes.

Conclusion

The study highlights the importance of collaboration and global research efforts in improving predictability and outcomes in translational research. By drawing on diverse perspectives and experiences, the potential for success in specific research activities is expected to increase. Overall, the study emphasizes the need for a more connected and coordinated approach to biomedical research to enhance its impact on health improvement.

records.title: Current applications and challenges of artificial intelligence applied to diagnostics in pediatric musculoskeletal imaging.

content.title: Current applications and challenges of artificial intelligence applied to diagnostics in pediatric musculoskeletal imaging.
content.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in pediatric musculoskeletal imaging has undergone significant expansion over the past few years. Until recently, the use of AI was limited to evaluating bone age and opportunistically assessing the bone health index. Currently, validated AI software for commercial use includes the detection of appendicular fractures, automated measurement of scoliosis, assessment of lower limb length discrepancy, and assessment of developing hip dysplasia. For other applications, further work is needed. Diagnostic accuracy for detecting rib and vertebral fractures in children using AI is currently not satisfactory; however, future research using enhanced deep learning is projected to address these limitations. The implementation of other applications of diagnostic AI in pediatric musculoskeletal imaging for non-accidental trauma, bone dysplasia, and tumor assessment is hindered by the lack of large pediatric datasets, which would require multicenter collaborations. This paper aims to succinctly outline the present clinical applications of AI in the pediatric musculoskeletal field, while elucidating existing possibilities, limitations, and future needs and prospects.

records.title: Virtual reality training for gait disorders in Parkinson's disease: a bibliometric and visual analysis of hotspots and trends using CiteSpace and VOSviewer.

content.title: Virtual reality training for gait disorders in Parkinson's disease: a bibliometric and visual analysis of hotspots and trends using CiteSpace and VOSviewer.
content.abstract:
Background

This study systematically reviews the current status, hotspot distribution, and developmental trends of virtual reality (VR) training for improving gait disorders in Parkinson's disease (PD).

Aim

To map the global intellectual landscape and emerging frontiers of VR training for PD gait disorders (primary objective), while identifying developmental gaps in Chinese research through cross-database comparative analysis (secondary objective).

Methods

Relevant literature published between 2008 and 2025 was retrieved from the Web of Science, PubMed, and CNKI databases. Ultimately, 535 English and 18 Chinese articles were included. CiteSpace and VOSviewer were used to conduct visual analyses of publication volume, cooperation networks (countries, authors, and institutions), keyword co-occurrence, clustering, and burst terms.

Results

English publication volume grew steadily, peaking between 2020 and 2025, whereas Chinese literature yielded only 18 articles (averaging fewer than three annually). The United States (108 papers) occupies the core position in the national cooperation network. China ranks third in publication volume (42 papers) but lacks extensive international collaboration. English keywords focused on "virtual reality," "gait," "balance," and "augmented reality," while Chinese keywords centered on similar core concepts. Burst term analysis indicates that research frontiers have shifted from "physical therapy" and "neuroplasticity" toward intelligent, remote, and personalized directions, such as "wearable sensors," "telerehabilitation," and "deep learning."

Discussion

VR training for PD gait disorders represents an expanding global research domain. Under strictly applied database parameters, cross-linguistic analysis reveals distinct thematic focuses rather than a baseline disparity. International English literature predominantly addresses technical frontier iterations, while Chinese-language publications demonstrate a highly specialized path dedicated to localized clinical application and efficacy verification. Future studies should strengthen multi-center cross-linguistic collaboration, emphasize precision rehabilitation and neural mechanisms, and promote personalized telerehabilitation interventions.

records.title: Mapping applications and evaluations of LLM-enabled AI chatbots for health purposes: a scoping review.

content.title: Mapping applications and evaluations of LLM-enabled AI chatbots for health purposes: a scoping review.
content.abstract:
Background

Large Language Model (LLM)-enabled artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly shaping health communication by mediating how patients, health professionals, researchers, and health institutions seek, interpret, produce, and act on health information. Existing reviews have largely focused on a single stakeholder group or clinical domain, leaving unclear how these systems are applied and evaluated across stakeholder groups and health purposes.

Objective

This scoping review mapped empirical studies of LLM-enabled AI chatbot applications and evaluations for health purposes across four stakeholder groups: the public or patients, health professionals, health researchers and students, and health institutions. We characterized the purposes and evidence patterns associated with these applications and evaluations.

Methods

We searched nine databases for peer-reviewed, English-language empirical studies available through July 2025. After screening, 286 articles were coded for study characteristics, methodology, evidence type, chatbot modality, LLM type, health topic, stakeholder group, and health purpose.

Results

The included articles were published between 2023 and 2025. Most examined general-purpose LLMs (n = 267, 93.4%). Studies were concentrated in the United States and China and primarily examined text-based chatbots. Noncommunicable or chronic diseases and general health information were the most common health topics. Ten health-related purposes were identified across four stakeholder groups and two umbrella categories. Public-facing applications involved the general public or patients and encompassed four purposes: (1) seeking health information, (2) symptom assessment and self-care management, (3) emotional support, and (4) preventive and transitional care support. Professional and organizational applications involved health professionals, health researchers and students, and health institutions, and encompassed six purposes: (5) clinical decision support, (6) improving administrative efficiency, (7) supporting patient interaction and doctor-patient communication, (8) enhancing continuing education, (9) facilitating health research, and (10) institutional workflow support and care navigation.

Conclusion

This review provides a stakeholder-purpose mapping of AI chatbot applications and evaluations in health care. The evidence base is concentrated in text-based, lower-acuity, and information-oriented contexts and derives primarily from output evaluations and self-reported perceptions or use. Key gaps concern institutional integration and governance, higher-stakes and longitudinal contexts, and evidence across populations, languages, and interaction modalities.

records.title: Association between the geriatric nutritional risk index and postoperative delirium: a meta-analysis.

content.title: Association between the geriatric nutritional risk index and postoperative delirium: a meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Malnutrition has been suggested as an important contributor to postoperative delirium (POD). The geriatric nutritional risk index (GNRI), a simple indicator based on serum albumin and body weight, has been increasingly evaluated in surgical patients.
