Five databases, including PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus, were searched up to November 2025 to identify randomized controlled trials measuring the effect of different ball sports on the subdomains of EF among children and adolescents. Paired analyses and network meta-analyses were conducted using the random-effects model.

Results

This study included 12 studies with five ball sports interventions. Ball sports showed domain-specific effects on EF in children and adolescents. The surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) reveals that football may be a potentially effective intervention for improving the accuracy rate of inhibitory control (SUCRA = 76.69%). For working memory, ball sports did not consistently enhance accuracy, with the control condition showing the highest ranking (SUCRA = 80.93%). In contrast, tennis exhibited the greatest likelihood of improving reaction time (SUCRA = 99.99%). Table tennis may be a potentially effective intervention for improving reaction time of cognitive flexibility (SUCRA = 99.97%). Sensitivity analyses restricted to typically developing samples revealed notable changes in network structures and SUCRA rankings for inhibitory control accuracy, inhibitory control reaction time, and cognitive flexibility accuracy.

Conclusion

Different ball sports demonstrated varying effects across executive function subdomains. However, the findings for inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility were highly dependent on sample composition and lacked robustness, whereas those for working memory were relatively stable. Due to limited evidence and high heterogeneity, the results should be interpreted with caution.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251038836.

records.title: Association of the Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio and Prognosis After Endovascular Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Association of the Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio and Prognosis After Endovascular Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background and purpose

Stress hyperglycemia (SH) is prevalent in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). The stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR), calculated as the fasting blood glucose (FBG)/glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) ratio, has been widely used to evaluate SH. However, the correlation between SHR and clinical outcomes in AIS patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) following endovascular treatment (EVT, including mechanical thrombectomy, contact aspiration, intra-arterial thrombolysis, excluding intravenous thrombolysis) remains unclear. This study aimed to perform a meta-analysis to investigate the association between SHR and clinical outcomes in EVT-treated AIS patients with LVO.

Methods

A comprehensive literature search was conducted across multiple databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, to identify studies investigating the association between SHR and clinical outcomes. The entire study was executed in strict adherence to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) guidelines. References were screened based on pre-specified inclusion and exclusion criteria, and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) was rigorously applied to assess potential bias risks in the selected studies. RevMan 5.3 software was utilized for performing meta-analyses on the included literature.

Results

A total of 10 studies met the inclusion criteria, and 3646 AIS patients who underwent EVT were included in this analysis. The meta-analysis results demonstrated a higher SHR was associated with an increased risk of poor outcomes (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 3-6) at 90 days (odds ratio [OR] = 2.65, 95% CI: 2.30-3.06, p < 0.001), mortality (OR = 2.62, 95% CI: 1.81-3.79, p < 0.001), intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) (OR = 1.53, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.27-1.85, p < 0.001), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) (OR = 2.05, 95% CI: 1.27-3.30, p < 0.003) after EVT.

Conclusion

A higher SHR may increase the occurrence of poor outcomes, mortality, ICH, and sICH in AIS patients caused by LVO after EVT. SHR is associated with poor prognosis in AIS patients caused by LVO after EVT.

records.title: Retinopathy of prematurity among infants in East Africa: a systematic review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Retinopathy of prematurity among infants in East Africa: a systematic review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Aim

To evaluate the pooled magnitude of retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) among infants' populations in East Africa.

Methods

A literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, Scopus, and African Journals Online to identify studies from East African published up to August 2025 that reported the magnitude of ROP and its associated factors. The quality of the included cohort and cross-sectional studies was assessed using a modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. A random-effects Meta-analysis was used to estimate the pooled magnitude of ROP and adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for associated factors, with results presented using 95% confidence intervals (CI). Heterogeneity among studies was assessed using the I² statistic, and subgroup analysis and meta-regression were performed to explore its sources. Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and Egger's regression test.

Results

A total of 11 studies were included. The pooled magnitude of ROP in East Africa was 18% (95%CI: 13%-24%, I 2=95.77%). The Meta-analysis result showed that infants who received oxygen therapy (pooled OR=4.61, 95%CI: 1.88-7.33), neonates with birth weight less than 1500 g (pooled OR=5.82, 95%CI: 2.89-8.75), and respiratory distress syndrome (pooled OR=3.92, 95%CI: 2.54-5.29) were factors associated with ROP.

Conclusion

ROP is a significant public health concern in East Africa, affecting nearly one in five preterm infants. Policymakers and healthcare providers should prioritize evidence-based interventions targeting the prevention and early detection of ROP to mitigate its long-term impact on childhood blindness.

records.title: Accuracy of Chatbot-Based Health Advice Related to Traumatic Dental Injuries: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
records.publisher: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology

content.title: Accuracy of Chatbot-Based Health Advice Related to Traumatic Dental Injuries: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background/aims

The growing use of generative artificial intelligence, especially chatbots, has motivated researchers to test the accuracy of health advice provided. Though there are studies comparing chatbot health advice for traumatic dental injuries (TDI), variable results have been reported. Hence, this systematic review aimed to assess contemporary chatbots for their ability to accurately and reliably provide responses to different types of questions related to emergency care of TDI.

Methods

The protocol was developed using the Cochrane Handbook and the Chatbot-Assessment-Reporting-Tool (CHART) statement and registered in the Open Science Framework. A literature search, based on the research question, was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Web of Science on September 19th, 2025, without any limitations. Screening of titles and abstracts and later full text, and data extraction were performed. These steps were followed by qualitative synthesis and meta-analysis. The quality of studies was assessed using their compliance with CHART.

Results

The review included 10 articles published in 2024 and 2025. Seven contemporary chatbots were evaluated with different themes and types of questions. Eight of the studies showed good compliance with CHART (≥ 75%). The overall pooled accuracy was 65% (95% CI 52%-78%, I2 = 88%) in ChatGPT-3.5, 79% (95% CI 61%-93%, I2 = 88.8%) in ChatGPT-4.0, and 70% (95% CI 60%-79%, I2 = 86.4%) in Gemini.

Conclusion

Overall accuracy of chatbot-generated advice was moderate, with substantial variation depending on the type of questions assessed. The meta-analysis demonstrated a suggestive trend of higher accuracy for ChatGPT-4.0, followed by Gemini, Copilot P, and ChatGPT-3.5. However, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical reliability, as even limited inaccuracies in emergency dental trauma advice may contribute to delayed or inappropriate management and adverse outcomes.

records.title: AI-driven ECG diagnostics: A game-changer for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. A systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

content.title: AI-driven ECG diagnostics: A game-changer for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. A systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a common inherited cardiovascular disorder that may cause serious complications. Accurate diagnosis of HCM is essential to mitigate adverse outcomes. The electrocardiogram (ECG), combined with advancements in machine learning (ML), presents a promising alternative for HCM diagnosis and this systematic review aimed to assess ECG-ML performance.

Objectives

This study aims to evaluate diagnostic accuracy of ECG-ML.

Methods

A search was conducted across five major electronic databases. Studies were included if they assessed ML algorithms for diagnosing HCM using ECG data. Bivariate random-effects meta-analysis was employed to pool diagnostic metrics, and subgroup analyses were performed to explore heterogeneity.

Results

A total of 21 studies were included. The pooled area under curve was 0.964 (95% CI 0.906-0.979) Sensitivity and specificity were 0.914 (95% CI 0.847-0.953) and 0.965 (95% CI 0.889-0.989), respectively. The diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) was 250.796, and the overall accuracy was 0.959 (95% CI 0.893-0.985). Heterogeneity was observed (I² > 90%). Subgroup analyses indicated variations in diagnostic performance based on ML model type, validation methods, and geographic origin. Quality concerns were found.

Conclusion

ML models demonstrated exceptional diagnostic accuracy in identifying HCM from ECG data, showing potential as effective diagnostic tools in resource-limited settings and primary care. However, heterogeneity and quality concerns highlight the need for standardized ML development and validation. Future research should focus on addressing these limitations, exploring explainable AI methods, and conducting to ensure clinical applicability.

records.title: Addition of immunotherapy to perioperative chemotherapy for resectable gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a meta-analysis of phase 2/3 trials.

content.title: Addition of immunotherapy to perioperative chemotherapy for resectable gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a meta-analysis of phase 2/3 trials.
content.abstract:
Background

The integration of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with perioperative chemotherapy (CT) has become a major focus of clinical research in resectable gastric or gastroesophageal junction (G/GEJ) cancer. Recent phase 2 and 3 trials have reported disparate outcomes, generating considerable debate. To synthesize this evidence, we conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of adding ICIs to CT in this setting.

Methods

A systematic literature search of PubMed and major conference proceedings was conducted up to August 15, 2025. Efficacy outcomes included summary relative risks (RRs) for pathological complete response (pCR) and R0 resection rate, and hazard ratios (HRs) for event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS). Safety was assessed using RRs for treatment-related adverse events (AEs).

Results

Four trials (one phase 2 [NEOSUMMIT-01], one phase 2/3 [DANTE], and two phase 3 [KEYNOTE-585, MATTERHORN]), encompassing 2,358 patients, were included. The addition of ICIs to CT significantly improved pCR (RR: 2.80; 95% CI: 1.68-4.67), EFS (HR: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.67-0.87), and OS (HR: 0.78; 95% CI: 0.61-0.99), although it did not increase the R0 resection rate. Regarding safety, the combination did not increase the risk of overall grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs. However, it was associated with a significantly higher risk of grade 3-5 immune-related AEs (RR: 2.88; 95% CI: 1.95-4.24) and treatment-related serious AEs (RR: 1.14; 95% CI: 1.01-1.28).

Conclusion

The addition of ICIs to perioperative CT confers significant improvements in pCR, EFS, and OS in resectable G/GEJ cancer, with a generally manageable safety profile. However, longer follow-up is required to validate survival benefits, and the increased risk of immune-related toxicity underscores the need for administration in specialized centers. These findings suggest that perioperative chemo-immunotherapy is a promising treatment strategy, though its definitive role awaits confirmation from ongoing phase 3 trials.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420251131385.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cardiothoracic Surgery: Promises, Failures, and the Gap to Clinical Reality.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cardiothoracic Surgery: Promises, Failures, and the Gap to Clinical Reality.
content.abstract:
Background

The growing interest in artificial intelligence (AI) in cardiothoracic surgery has led to a substantial increase in scientific publications, although its integration into routine clinical practice remains limited. Despite encouraging developments in several areas of surgical care, the clinical benefits of many proposed applications have yet to be established.

Objective

This review critically examines the discrepancy between the reported capabilities of AI-based technologies and their implementation in clinical cardiothoracic surgical practice, with particular emphasis on the factors limiting their broader adoption.

Methods

A semi-systematic literature review covering publications from January 2018 through September 2026 was conducted to examine the development, validation, and clinical application of AI-based tools across the preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative stages of cardiothoracic surgical care. Particular attention was given to methodological limitations, external validation, and barriers to clinical implementation.

Key findings

Although several AI models have demonstrated promising performance in retrospective studies and controlled research settings, evidence supporting their reliability and clinical utility in routine practice remains limited. Important challenges include insufficient external and prospective validation, variable generalizability across clinical settings, limited model interpretability, and difficulties integrating AI-based systems into established surgical and intensive care workflows. Regulatory requirements, technical infrastructure, and human factors represent additional barriers to implementation.

Conclusions

The clinical translation of AI in cardiothoracic surgery requires more than improvements in algorithmic performance. Greater emphasis on robust external validation, prospective clinical evaluation, workflow integration, and appropriate regulatory oversight is necessary to establish the safety, effectiveness, and practical value of these technologies. Addressing these challenges will be essential for translating advances in AI research into meaningful improvements in cardiothoracic surgical care.

records.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.

content.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
content.abstract:
Objectives

We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome.

Methods

We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model.

Results

The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR).

Conclusions

Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Electrocardiography in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit: Implications for Coronary Intervention Decision-Making.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Electrocardiography in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit: Implications for Coronary Intervention Decision-Making.
content.abstract: Coronary intervention in the cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) demands rapid, accurate diagnosis and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to guide revascularization decisions. The 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) remains the most immediately available diagnostic tool in this setting; however, conventional interpretation is limited by inter-observer variability, ventilator-induced artifact, and inherent insensitivity for atypical coronary occlusion presentations. Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered ECG analysis has emerged as a promising adjunct to interventional cardiology practice, with the potential to support automated detection of occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI)-including cases missed by conventional STEMI criteria-while simultaneously providing multiparametric assessment of left ventricular function, hemodynamic status, and electrolyte derangements relevant to procedural safety. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the clinical utility of AI-ECG with direct relevance to coronary intervention decision-making, focusing on: (1) OMI and STEMI detection and the potential reduction in false catheterization laboratory activations; (2) pre- and peri-procedural risk stratification using AI-ECG-derived ventricular function and diastolic dysfunction parameters; (3) periprocedural arrhythmia monitoring; and (4) electrolyte derangement screening relevant to procedural safety. Composite illustrative scenarios based on the authors' CICU experience describe how the ECG Buddy AI-ECG system (QCG platform, Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety-approved) may support the recognition of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and the decision to proceed with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in mechanically ventilated patients with septic shock-a scenario in which conventional diagnostic pathways are often confounded. These scenarios are presented for illustration only and do not constitute evidence of clinical benefit. Retrospective single-center studies in large unselected CICU populations (n > 9000, Mayo Clinic series) have shown that AI-ECG is independently associated with mortality beyond conventional echocardiographic parameters, supporting its potential role as a decision-support tool. Whether AI-ECG-assisted decision-making improves clinical outcomes in coronary intervention remains to be established in prospective studies.

records.title: A four-domain framework for AI-enabled mobile health: from sensing to equitable governance.

content.title: A four-domain framework for AI-enabled mobile health: from sensing to equitable governance.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely expected to strengthen mobile health (mHealth) responses to the dual burden of non-communicable and infectious disease, yet translation into demonstrable population health benefit remains limited. This narrative review conceptualizes AI-mHealth as the mobile and wearable layer of an Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled connected health ecosystem. Because the literature has largely examined sensing, modeling, and implementation as discrete problems, the dependencies that govern system-level utility remain poorly characterized. We therefore appraise the evidence across four linked domains: Sensing, Inference, Intervention, and Governance. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE and the Web of Science Core Collection from October 2015 to September 2026. Sensing performance depended on device and measurement context. Wrist-worn photoplethysmography showed no consistent skin-tone-related error at rest, whereas error in darker skin tones exceeded that in lighter skin tones more than fourfold at higher exercise intensities. Inference models improved risk stratification but lacked the interpretability required to support clinical accountability, and model compression for on-device deployment degraded subgroup performance unevenly. Just-in-time adaptive interventions improved proximal response, although effect durability varied across microrandomized trials, and remote heart failure management has not yet demonstrated a consistent effect on readmission. Algorithmic bias, the digital divide, deficiencies in data stewardship and cybersecurity, limited human oversight, and regulatory latency form a mutually reinforcing system of risk across the AI-mHealth lifecycle. Our principal finding is an asymmetry: upstream limitations propagate downstream automatically, whereas their correction requires deliberate institutional design. We propose an operational roadmap of four implementation phases, from technical readiness to accountability at scale. Each phase is mapped to the framework domains it engages and to the specific Sustainable Development Goal 3 targets it serves, spanning communicable disease screening, chronic disease management, workforce capacity, and universal coverage. Aggregate accuracy concealed reliability loss in the subgroups most in need of intervention, and the roadmap therefore makes subgroup-level equity auditing a condition of deployment.

records.title: Digital Twins in Oncology: Current Evidence, Multiscale Modeling Approaches, and Challenges in Clinical Translation-A Narrative Review.

content.title: Digital Twins in Oncology: Current Evidence, Multiscale Modeling Approaches, and Challenges in Clinical Translation-A Narrative Review.
content.abstract: Digital Twin (DT), a dynamic simulation technology derived from the engineering field, has been deeply integrated into the field of tumor precision medicine, empowered by both multi-omics technologies and artificial intelligence. It offers a novel approach to overcoming the limitations of traditional paradigms in tumor research, diagnosis, and treatment. This article reviews the full-scale application system of tumor DT, spanning from the molecular to the individual level, and constructs a progressive simulation architecture of "virtual cell-virtual knockout/virtual overexpression-virtual organoid-virtual patient". The virtual cell enables the in silico representation of tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment, serving as the fundamental unit for dissecting molecular mechanisms. Virtual knockout/overexpression provides non-invasive, high-throughput methods for target prioritization, significantly shortening research and development cycles. The virtual organoid achieves computational reconstruction of the three-dimensional (3D) tumor microenvironment, bridging the gap between single-cell and individual-scale simulations. The virtual patient, in turn, supports personalized therapeutic decision-making and virtual clinical trials. By synthesizing the latest research findings in the field, this article delineates the technical pathways, primary modeling tools, and representative empirical cases for each application tier. It further provides an in-depth analysis of core challenges, including multi-source data heterogeneity, insufficient model accuracy and interpretability, and obstacles to clinical translation. Corresponding solutions, such as data standardization, cross-scale technology integration, and interdisciplinary collaboration between medicine and engineering, are proposed. The aim is to provide a comprehensive reference for leveraging DT to advance tumor research and facilitate its translation into clinical practice.

records.title: Differential scanning calorimetry and artificial intelligence for analytical profiling of disease-related plasma thermograms.

content.title: Differential scanning calorimetry and artificial intelligence for analytical profiling of disease-related plasma thermograms.
content.abstract: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) is a systems-level thermodynamic tool for probing disease-related changes in complex biological fluids, yet clinical translation is hindered by challenges in thermogram interpretation, reproducibility, and data integration. DSC captures heat capacity transitions from multistate protein unfolding, reflecting collective stability landscapes of the plasma proteome. Pathological conditions can induce reproducible thermogram distortions, suggesting their utility as ensemble biomarkers beyond conventional scalar descriptors. Recent advances in ultrasensitive and microfluidic DSC have improved stability and reduced sample needs, while artificial intelligence enables extraction of distributed calorimetric features beyond melting temperature and enthalpy. Machine learning strategies-including statistical, kernel-based, deep learning, and physics-informed frameworks-help identify informative thermodynamic patterns. This review integrates thermodynamic principles, data-driven analytics, and clinical studies to assess DSC's capabilities and limitations. We further propose practical standardization and minimum-reporting frameworks for DSC acquisition, preprocessing, AI model development, and validation to improve reproducibility and cross-study comparability. Persistent issues such as inter-laboratory variability, cohort heterogeneity, small datasets, and regulatory hurdles continue to restrict routine use. Overall, combining DSC with AI offers a promising analytical framework for extracting clinically meaningful thermodynamic insights and advancing disease characterization.

records.title: A Review of Mechanistic and Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Models for Predicting Pesticide Fate and Transport in Soil and Water

content.title: A Review of Mechanistic and Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Models for Predicting Pesticide Fate and Transport in Soil and Water
content.abstract: Global pesticide use exceeded 3.7 million tonnes in 2023, and residues that persist beyond the treated field drive diffuse soil, surface water, and groundwater contamination linked to ecological harm and an estimated 150,000 pesticide poisoning deaths annually. Because field monitoring of pesticide fate across every soil, climate, and hydrological setting is logistically and financially infeasible at regulatory scale, predictive modelling has become the primary tool for estimating environmental concentrations and associated risk. This review traces the development of the field from traditional process-based mechanisms to hybrid AI frameworks by synthesizing 81 peer-reviewed and technical sources from an initial pool of 1,450 records screened across Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect (2005–2026). We look at the physicochemical and degradation principles that determine the fate of pesticides; the deterministic, mechanistic, process-based, empirical, and statistical models that support the current regulatory risk assessment; the hydrological and transport models that function at the soil profile to watershed scale; and the expanding array of machine learning, deep learning, fuzzy logic, GIS, remote sensing, and IoT-enabled techniques that are transforming precision agriculture and prediction. Case studies from India and other countries demonstrate real-world uses in addition to ongoing limitations in data accessibility and cross-context transferability. We point out important gaps, such as persistent data scarcity in low- and middle-income regions, limited coupling of fate models to downscaled climate projections, and inadequate integration of explainable AI to foster regulatory trust. We identify calibration and validation, particularly probabilistic uncertainty quantification, as essential to the responsible use of both conventional and data-driven models. We conclude that creating accurate, transferable pesticide prediction systems that support the Sustainable Development Goals and safeguard human and environmental health requires combining mechanistic understanding with hybrid, physics-informed AI and climate-resilient precision agriculture technologies.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cardiovascular Disease: Current Applications, Methodological Challenges, and Clinical Translation.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cardiovascular Disease: Current Applications, Methodological Challenges, and Clinical Translation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is increasingly being investigated for cardiovascular diagnosis, risk stratification, and prognostic assessment, leveraging electrocardiography, cardiovascular imaging, electronic health records, wearable devices, and molecular data. This review summarizes current AI applications in ischemic heart disease, acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, arrhythmias, and structural cardiovascular disease, and critically examines the methodological requirements for clinical translation. Particular attention is given to model taxonomy, data leakage, overfitting, external validation, calibration, dataset shift, explainability, clinical utility, privacy, cybersecurity, and regulatory considerations. Current evidence shows that AI can identify clinically relevant patterns and may complement conventional cardiovascular assessment; however, high performance in retrospective or selected datasets does not necessarily translate into improved patient outcomes. Therefore, robust patient-level data separation, independent external and prospective validation, calibration assessment, workflow evaluation, and post-deployment monitoring are essential. Emerging multimodal, hybrid, and foundation-model approaches may further improve cardiovascular prediction, but their clinical value requires rigorous evaluation. Currently, AI should primarily be regarded as a complementary decision-support tool rather than a replacement for established diagnostic or prognostic standards.

records.title: Physical Activity in Relation to University Students' Large Language Model Dependence: Moderated Mediation Effect Between Self-Control and Exploratory Learning Ability.

content.title: Physical Activity in Relation to University Students' Large Language Model Dependence: Moderated Mediation Effect Between Self-Control and Exploratory Learning Ability.
content.abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, concerns about severe dependence on large language models (LLMs) are increasing among university students. This cross-sectional study aims to examine the underlying association between physical activity and LLM dependence, especially the mediating role of self-control and the moderating role of exploratory learning ability underlying them. Using stratified cluster sampling, 602 university students in China were recruited and then completed several standardized measurements, including the Physical Activity Rating Scale-3, Self-Control Scale, Large Language Model Dependence Scale, and Exploratory Learning Scale, and relevant data were analyzed using SPSS 27.0 and PROCESS Model 58. The present work discloses that physical activity was positively correlated with self-control, yet negatively correlated with LLM dependence, and its direct conditional association with LLM dependence was non-significant, whereas the indirect association via self-control was significant. Exploratory learning ability could moderate both the positive association between physical activity and self-control and the negative association between self-control and LLM dependence, and the indirect association between physical activity and LLM dependence via self-control would also be significantly moderated by exploratory learning ability, while this moderating effect might exist only at lower levels of exploratory learning ability. These findings clearly identify self-control as a potential psychological pathway and exploratory learning ability as a boundary condition of physical activity and LLM dependence. The models only explained 8.8% of the variance in self-control and 19.6% of the variance in LLM dependence, so the discovery should be only interpreted as preliminary associations rather than causal evidence.

records.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.

content.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed for detecting microbial and chemical hazards in food, but laboratory accuracies are rarely reproduced in routine use. This structured narrative review examined whether reported performance is traceable, independently validated, and transferable to operational settings. Eight bibliographic databases and seven institutional routes were searched for English-language records published from January 2018 to May 2026, and we screened the records; the final corpus comprised 76 sources (53 journal articles, 9 conference papers, 2 preprints, and 12 institutional or regulatory documents). Seven primary studies supporting the quantitative evidence were appraised individually against 11 indicators, including test-set independence, external validation, and leakage control. Physical-hazard inspection and narrow-matrix spectral grading had the strongest deployment evidence, whereas microbial and chemical screening remained at laboratory or pilot scale. Among the appraised studies, the most credible estimates came from physically or temporally independent test sets, and no sensor-based study evaluated transfer to another instrument or laboratory. Deep learning showed clear advantages for image-based tasks but not consistently for small-sample spectral calibration. Adoption is limited mainly by validation design, recalibration burden, false-alarm costs, and the absence of a regulatory pathway rather than by accuracy. AI is best positioned as a screening and decision-support layer linked to confirmatory testing and human oversight.

records.title: Effects of exercise intervention parameters on anxiety symptoms in adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

content.title: Effects of exercise intervention parameters on anxiety symptoms in adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
content.abstract:
Objective

This meta-analysis aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of exercise interventions (including aerobic exercise, Yoga, and Tai Chi) on anxiety symptoms in adolescents and to explore the moderating roles of intervention parameters.

Methods

Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of exercise interventions on adolescent anxiety symptoms were searched in PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang Database, and VIP Information up to October 15, 2025. The Cochrane Risk of Bias tool was used for quality assessment. Meta-analysis, subgroup analyses, sensitivity analysis, and publication bias assessment were performed using Review Manager 5.4.

Results

Twelve RCTs with a total of 1,874 participants were included. The overall effect size was small but statistically significant [SMD = -0.30, 95% CI (-0.60, -0.01), P = 0.04], with substantial heterogeneity (I 2 = 87%, P < 0.00001). Subgroup analyses suggested that intervention effects may vary by exercise type, session duration, weekly frequency, and total intervention duration. Exploratory findings indicated that interventions with 30-min sessions, five times per week, and longer total duration (~45 weeks) were associated with larger reductions in anxiety symptoms. However, these subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the limited number of studies per subgroup.

Conclusions

Exercise-based interventions may reduce anxiety symptoms in adolescents, although the effect magnitude is small and the evidence is limited by substantial heterogeneity. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggest that exercise parameters may influence intervention outcomes, but no definitive optimal prescription can be established based on the current evidence. Future research with standardized protocols and larger samples is warranted.PROSPERO Registration: CRD420251265936.

records.title: Meta-analysis and dose-response analysis of low-temperature stress effects on rice yield and physiological responses.

content.title: Meta-analysis and dose-response analysis of low-temperature stress effects on rice yield and physiological responses.
content.abstract: Low-temperature stress is a major environmental constraint on rice yield stability, considerable variation remains in the reported direction and magnitude of these effects. In this study, we conducted a systematic meta-analysis combined with dose-response analysis to evaluate the effects of low-temperature stress on rice yield formation, photosynthetic capacity, and physiological responses. The results showed that low-temperature stress significantly reduced yield-related traits in rice, with yield per plant and pollen viability decreasing by 10.58% and 21.75%, respectively. Photosynthetic performance was also markedly affected, as net photosynthetic rate (Pn), transpiration rate (Tr), and stomatal conductance (Gs) decreased by 26.67%, 10.93%, and 31.00%, respectively, while intercellular CO<sub>2</sub> concentration (Ci) increased by 5.75%. Low-temperature stress also significantly induced the accumulation of osmotic regulatory substances and aggravated oxidative damage. Subgroup analysis and meta-regression indicated that the effects of low-temperature stress were jointly regulated by growth stage, stress temperature, and stress duration. Specifically, yield responses were more sensitive at the booting stage and heading-flowering stage, while Pn showed more pronounced responses to severe low temperature and prolonged stress. Dose-response analysis showed that most traits exhibited response turning points around 24 °C. Overall, this study quantitatively revealed the associations among yield reduction, photosynthetic inhibition, and physiological homeostasis imbalance in rice under low-temperature stress, providing comprehensive evidence for understanding the response patterns of rice to low temperature.

records.title: Integrating <i>In silico</i> perturbation with multilayer omics to decode regulatory networks in cancer immunity: a new frontier in precision oncology.

content.title: Integrating <i>In silico</i> perturbation with multilayer omics to decode regulatory networks in cancer immunity: a new frontier in precision oncology.
content.abstract: The traditional paradigm of linking single genes to individual phenotypes is being replaced by a systems-level framework to understand the complexity of the tumor microenvironment. In this context, in silico knockout has emerged as a powerful computational approach to predict system-wide responses to genetic or cellular perturbations. This review summarizes how multilayer regulatory information across the genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome can be integrated into computational models for virtual perturbation analysis. We outline major multi-omics data sources, including bulk, single-cell, and spatial omics, and emphasize how these data are transformed into model-compatible inputs such as constraint-based matrices and latent embeddings. We then discuss the evolution of in silico knockout methodologies, from genome-scale metabolic models and flux balance analysis to advanced deep learning frameworks that enable the prediction of non-linear and unseen perturbations. The integration of spatial transcriptomics further extends these approaches to tissue-level modeling of cell-cell interactions. In tumor immunology, these methods facilitate the identification of immune regulatory genes, the analysis of immune evasion mechanisms, and the prioritization of therapeutic targets. Despite current challenges in multi-omics integration and biological complexity, in silico knockout provides a promising framework for advancing precision immunotherapy.

records.title: Association between early postnatal antibiotic exposure and bronchopulmonary dysplasia in very preterm infants: a meta-analysis.

content.title: Association between early postnatal antibiotic exposure and bronchopulmonary dysplasia in very preterm infants: a meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

Very preterm infants are at high risk of infection due to their immature immune systems, and empirical antibiotic therapy is commonly initiated shortly after birth. However, excessive or unnecessary antibiotic exposure may adversely affect organ development and long-term outcomes. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the association between early postnatal antibiotic exposure and bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) as well as other adverse outcomes in very preterm infants, to provide evidence for optimizing antibiotic stewardship in neonatal care.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Wiley Online Library, and the Cochrane Library database were systematically searched from inception to March 2026. Observational cohort studies comparing early postnatal antibiotic exposure with no exposure or short-term exposure were included. The primary outcome was bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), and secondary outcomes included necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), mortality, and late-onset sepsis (LOS). Meta-analysis was performed using fixed-effects or random-effects models to calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity analysis and Egger's test were conducted to assess the robustness of the results and potential publication bias. For outcomes with significant publication bias, the trim-and-fill method was applied.

Results

A total of 11 studies was included. Pooled analysis showed that early postnatal antibiotic exposure was associated with an increased risk of BPD (OR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.12-1.85). In addition, the risks of NEC (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.09-1.28) and mortality (OR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.05-1.35) were significantly increased, while no statistically significant association was observed for late-onset sepsis (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.71-1.34). Sensitivity analyses indicated that the results were stable. Publication bias was detected for BPD and mortality; after trim-and-fill correction, the BPD result remained robust, whereas the mortality result warrants cautious interpretation.

Conclusion

Early postnatal antibiotic exposure is associated with an increased risk of BPD and several adverse outcomes in very preterm infants. Careful assessment of infection risk and optimization of antibiotic initiation and discontinuation strategies may help improve long-term outcomes in this population.

records.title: Efficacy and safety of acupuncture for dysphagia after radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy and safety of acupuncture for dysphagia after radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Acupuncture has been used as an adjunctive supportive intervention for various cancer-related symptoms. However, its efficacy and safety for dysphagia after radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma have not been systematically evaluated.

Objective

To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for dysphagia after radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The outcomes were post-treatment Water Swallowing Test (WST) scores, the proportion of patients achieving a favorable swallowing status, the clinical effective rate, videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS) outcomes, and Standardized Swallowing Assessment (SSA) scores.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Chinese Biomedical Literature Database, Wanfang Database, and VIP Database were searched from inception to March 2026. Eligible randomized controlled trials were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool. Meta-analyses were conducted using R software.

Results

Twelve randomized controlled trials including 863 patients were analyzed. Acupuncture reduced post-treatment WST scores compared with control interventions (MD = -0.78, 95% CI: -1.04 to -0.51). The clinical effective rate was also higher in the acupuncture group (RR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.08 to 1.27). Moreover, acupuncture improved VFSS outcomes (SMD = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.46 to 1.05), reduced SSA scores (MD = -7.65, 95% CI: -12.30 to -3.01), and improved quality of life and nutritional indicators. Safety reporting was limited, precluding definitive conclusions regarding the safety of acupuncture in this population.

Conclusion

Acupuncture may have a potential adjunctive role in improving swallowing function, swallowing-related quality of life, and nutritional indicators in patients with dysphagia after radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma. However, the evidence remains limited by small sample sizes, methodological limitations, and heterogeneity across outcomes. Larger, well-designed randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings and further clarify the clinical role of acupuncture.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261371533.

records.title: Comparison of the efficacy of neuromodulation techniques based on corticospinal excitability in improving exercise-induced fatigue in athletes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Comparison of the efficacy of neuromodulation techniques based on corticospinal excitability in improving exercise-induced fatigue in athletes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Exercise-induced fatigue (EIF) is a core problem in competitive sports, significantly affecting the training quality and performance of athletes. Neuromodulation techniques based on corticospinal excitability regulation-including both central and peripheral stimulation-offer a novel approach to EIF intervention; however, the comparative efficacy of different techniques remains unclear.

Objective

To compare the effects of various neuromodulation techniques on EIF in athletes using a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data, and VIP databases were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials comparing neuromodulation techniques with placebo/sham stimulation/blank control from database inception to June 2026. The Cochrane ROB-2 tool was used to assess risk of bias, and the CINeMA framework was applied to evaluate evidence quality. A Bayesian model was employed for network meta-analysis, with SUCRA values calculated to rank efficacy, and meta-regression was used to explore sources of heterogeneity.

Results

A total of 14 RCTs involving 756 athletes were included. The paired meta-analysis showed that neuromodulation techniques significantly reduced BLA levels and alleviated fatigue (MD = -0.47, 95% CI: -0.57, -0.38). Network meta-analysis indicated that TEAS combined with acupuncture ranked first in improving RPE (SUCRA = 99.3%), blood lactate (SUCRA = 96.3%), and BUN (SUCRA = 72.6%). CINeMA evaluation showed that most evidence was of low quality. Meta-regression revealed that the total number of stimulations negatively moderated the effect on blood lactate (P = 0.001), and intervention type, risk of bias, and study design significantly influenced BUN outcomes (all P < 0.05).

Conclusion

TEAS combined with acupuncture may be associated with the most favorable SUCRA ranking, but this should be interpreted as exploratory for improving EIF in athletes. However, the overall quality of current evidence is low, and SUCRA rankings should be interpreted as exploratory. Future high-quality RCTs are needed to validate these findings and determine the optimal stimulation parameter ranges.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261446854.

records.title: Beyond the hype: navigating the real-world applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare.

content.title: Beyond the hype: navigating the real-world applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare.
content.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into healthcare signifies one of the most formidable and multifaceted advancements in contemporary medicine. The relentless pace of innovation necessitates a timely synthesis of the field's trajectory, critically evaluating both the promises and complexities of this ongoing transformation. This report aims to map the expansive terrain of AI's deployment across critical healthcare sectors, encompassing clinical decision support, diagnostic imaging, pharmaceutical innovation, biomedical research, and regulatory review. It begins with an analysis of the opportunities and challenges inherent in the real-world implementation of AI technologies, systematically categorizing their adoption and utilities into three core domains: (1) clinical informatics and healthcare delivery, (2) clinical sciences and therapeutic interventions, and (3) drug development and biomedical investigation. Thereafter, the discussion turns to AI's role within the regulatory landscape for drug and medical product reviews and approvals. Adopting a progressive outlook, the author formulates strategic recommendations aimed at surmounting potential barriers, thus facilitating the judicious, efficacious, and equitable integration of AI. Collectively, these analyses provide a narrative that highlights both the transformative potential and the pragmatic imperatives of deploying AI to improve human health.

records.title: Occupational burnout and professional efficacy in physical education: a multilevel meta-analysis of the job demands-resources model.

content.title: Occupational burnout and professional efficacy in physical education: a multilevel meta-analysis of the job demands-resources model.
content.abstract:
Introduction

This study aims to update, synthesize, and provide meta-analytical evidence of the associations between specific Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) dimensions and psychological outcomes (burnout and professional efficacy) among physical education (PE) teachers.

Methods

Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, the authors conducted a systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis. In May 2026, five major electronic databases, such as Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, PubMed, and EBSCOhost, were searched for peer-reviewed cross-sectional studies examining JD-R antecedent variables and specified psychological outcomes in PE teachers. Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria, with a combined sample of 4,341 participants and 77 effect sizes included in the four target pathways.

Results

Multilevel meta-analyses indicated a positive association between job demands and burnout (k = 17, r = 0.477, 95% CI [0.376, 0.568], p < 0.001) and a negative association between resources and burnout (k = 53, r = -0.342, 95% CI [-0.435, -0.241], p < 0.001). Exploratory resource-subgroup estimates were r = -0.350 for personal resources (k = 30, 95% CI [-0.523, -0.148], p = 0.002), r = -0.291 for organizational and social resources (k = 7, 95% CI [-0.541, 0.006], p = 0.053), and r = -0.343 for other work-related correlates (k = 16, 95% CI [-0.401, -0.282], p < 0.001). Exploratory country analyses indicated between-country differences, F(6, 46) = 4.476, p=0.0012. Neither resources nor demands were significantly associated with professional efficacy (k = 4, r = 0.246, p = 0.517; k = 3, r = -0.432, p = 0.111, respectively). Sensitivity checks confirm the results held.

Discussion

The magnitude and direction of the link between teaching environments and psychological outcomes depend on specific JD-R dimensions and local cultural contexts. These findings support associations of greater resources with lower burnout and greater demands with higher burnout. Resource-subgroup and country-level findings require cautious interpretation because of the limited number of independent studies.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420261385085, CRD420261385085.

records.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Discovery of Marine Antimicrobial Peptides: A Roadmap Integrating Omics Mining, Structure-Guided Diffusion Design, and Sustainable Aquaculture Translation.

content.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Discovery of Marine Antimicrobial Peptides: A Roadmap Integrating Omics Mining, Structure-Guided Diffusion Design, and Sustainable Aquaculture Translation.
content.abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) offer diverse antibacterial mechanisms, but candidate generation alone does not resolve the linked demands of potency, host safety, stability, manufacturability, and application-specific exposure. This review presents a roadmap that integrates two complementary computational routes for marine AMP discovery. De novo generation expands sequence space, whereas omics mining preserves biological provenance and enables recovery of encoded or encrypted peptides from marine organisms and microbiomes. Structure-guided diffusion is positioned as a selective third route when a defined target, motif, or stable structural template is available, rather than as a universal replacement for sequence-based AMP models. We further examine aquaculture as a translational setting in which efficacy must be evaluated together with salt and feed tolerance, environmental fate, tissue residues, resistance risk, and export-related requirements. Current evidence remains limited at the direct intersection of marine provenance and deep learning, particularly for target-conditioned structural design. We therefore propose an evidence-based workflow that links marine sequence resources, model selection, matched experimental validation, and application-specific deployment. This framework is intended to move marine AMP research from candidate prediction toward reproducible and testable translation.

records.title: Closed-loop neuromodulation: a paradigm shift in precision neuroscience for clinical and cognitive applications.

content.title: Closed-loop neuromodulation: a paradigm shift in precision neuroscience for clinical and cognitive applications.
content.abstract: Closed-loop neuromodulation systems are critically synthesized here with respect to their foundational principles, mechanistic underpinnings, and systematic classifications. This comprehensive survey covers their rapid research progress and expanding clinical applications, while rigorously exploring their emerging potential for cognitive augmentation. Concurrently, persistent challenges and future research directions are identified. The scope encompasses invasive, non-invasive, and peripheral techniques, with careful examination of their therapeutic utility in neurological and psychiatric disorders-including epilepsy, major depression, chronic pain syndromes, and movement disorders-alongside exploratory applications in cognitive enhancement among healthy individuals. Enabling technologies, such as advanced wireless biosensors, sophisticated AI-driven adaptive algorithms, and novel stimulation modalities, are critically assessed, juxtaposed with inherent challenges like robust biomarker validation, long-term device stability, and complex ethical considerations. Closed-loop neuromodulation systems have demonstrably achieved superior efficacy, enhanced personalization, and improved safety profiles compared to conventional open-loop paradigms. The accelerating pace of technological innovation is rapidly translating these advances from bench to bedside. This technology signifies a fundamental evolution in personalized medicine and offers substantial potential for cognitive optimization, necessitating concerted interdisciplinary collaboration to surmount extant challenges and ensure successful, responsible implementation.

records.title: AI-assisted history education in China: a secondary evidence map of psychological antecedents and learning outcomes.

content.title: AI-assisted history education in China: a secondary evidence map of psychological antecedents and learning outcomes.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Evidence on the use of artificial intelligence in Chinese history education remains fragmented. This study mapped the available secondary evidence and contextualized it with targeted corroboration of history-specific studies.

Methods

We analyzed a public bibliographic export of 1,063 records current to 1 April 2024 and conducted targeted full-text corroboration to identify history-education evidence beyond the original repository. After sequential screening, 30 records were retained for the contextual map. An expanded synonym audit was also performed to assess whether any direct history-education studies were missed.

Results

Nine records explicitly identified mainland China, Hong Kong, or Taiwan as the study setting, including five primary empirical studies. The synonym audit did not identify a direct history-education study in the repository. Targeted corroboration identified one 2025 mainland-China study of AI-assisted secondary-school history teaching, two systematic reviews describing broader history-education literature, and one adjacent cultural-heritage education study. In the regional subset, emotion/anxiety/cognitive-load outcomes were reported in five records, engagement in four, motivation and self-efficacy in three each, skills/competence in six, and knowledge and performance in five each.

Discussion

The repository should be interpreted as a contextual map of secondary evidence rather than a comprehensive estimate of the field. Overall, the evidence suggests emerging but still limited and heterogeneous attention to AI in Chinese history education.

records.title: Efficacy and safety of commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations combined with biomedicine for elderly patients with primary insomnia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

content.title: Efficacy and safety of commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations combined with biomedicine for elderly patients with primary insomnia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
content.abstract:
Introduction

The prevalence of primary insomnia among the elderly is steadily increasing; however, robust evidence supporting the efficacy and safety of combining commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations (CCPPs) with biomedicine therapy remains insufficient. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of CCPPs combined with biomedicine versus biomedicine therapy for primary insomnia in elderly patients, and to assess the certainty of the evidence via the GRADE framework and P-curve analysis.

Methods

Seven biomedical databases were searched (before November 2025) for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving elderly patients with primary insomnia. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2 by two researchers independently. Meta-analysis was performed using R software. Outcomes included Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), total clinical effectiveness rate, Sleep Dysfunction Rating Scale (SDRS), and adverse events. Robustness was evaluated via sensitivity, subgroup, and P-curve analyses.

Results

Meta-analysis suggested that combined therapy was associated with a lower PSQI score (MD = -2.09, 95% CI -2.62 to -1.57) and higher total clinical effectiveness rate (RR = 1.21, 95% CI 1.15-1.27) relative to monotherapy. The combination group also showed a lower risk of adverse events (RR = 0.47, 95% CI 0.36-0.61). However, P-curve analysis revealed notable discrepancies across outcomes: PSQI exhibited sufficient evidential value (Power = 99%), whereas the total clinical effectiveness rate lacked adequate evidential value (Power = 9%), implying potential publication bias. Subgroup analyses showed that heterogeneity decreased within the subgroup of patients with disease duration <1 year, although the between-subgroup difference did not reach statistical significance. The certainty of evidence was rated as "Moderate" for adverse events but "Low" to "Very Low" for efficacy outcomes.

Conclusion

In elderly patients with primary insomnia, combined treatment of CCPPs and biomedicine may help improve sleep quality and may reduce adverse events reported in clinical trials. However, due to methodological limitations, high heterogeneity and potential publication bias among the included trials, the certainty of the available evidence remains limited. Given insufficient evidential value, the reliability of the total clinical effectiveness rate is questionable, and clinicians should place greater emphasis on outcomes assessed using validated scales such as the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Further large-scale, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are needed to further verify these preliminary findings.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251186213, identifier: CRD420251186213.

records.title: Deep Learning for Real-Time Image Interpretation in Arthroscopy: A Systematic Review of Classification, Segmentation, and Detection Tasks.

content.title: Deep Learning for Real-Time Image Interpretation in Arthroscopy: A Systematic Review of Classification, Segmentation, and Detection Tasks.
content.abstract:
Background

Deep learning (DL) is increasingly applied to arthroscopic video for instrument recognition, anatomical segmentation, and intraoperative event detection. The performance, architectures, and real-time feasibility of these systems remain incompletely characterized. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the performance, architectures, and real-time feasibility of DL for classification, segmentation, and detection in arthroscopic video interpretation.

Methods

Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, PubMed/ MEDLINE, Ovid, and the Cochrane Library were searched (February 2025), supplemented by artificial intelligence-assisted queries (Elicit, Undermind). Eligible studies applied DL to arthroscopy for classification, segmentation, or detection with quantitative performance and/or inference speed. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted, and assessed quality using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2; the protocol was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews.

Results

Six studies met inclusion criteria (knee = 2, shoulder = 2, wrist = 1, non-site-specific bleeding = 1). Classification achieved high accuracy for instrument recognition (up to 99.1%, sensitivity = 0.988) and bleeding- frame detection (95.8%, sensitivity = 97.3%). Segmentation was strongest for large bony structures (Dice 0.79-0.89) and weakest for deformable tissues (meniscus Dice = 0.48). U-Net variants (U-Net++, DeepLab v3+) predominated with frequent transfer learning. Two studies achieved real-time inference (15-60 frames per second). Risk of bias was high across all studies.

Conclusion

Based on 6 heterogeneous studies, DL appears technically feasible for arthroscopic image interpretation, particularly instrument classification and osseous segmentation, though findings should be interpreted as preliminary. No study evaluated impact on surgical decision-making or patient outcomes, and none was deployed prospectively in live surgery. Translation will require multicentre datasets, standardized reporting, and prospective evaluation against clinically meaningful endpoints. Cite this article as: Lasslett C, Reddy R, Giritharan G, et al. Deep learning for real-time image interpretation in arthroscopy: a systematic review of classification, segmentation, and detection tasks. Eurasian J Med. 2026, 58(4), 1415, doi: 10.5152/ eurasianjmed.2026.261415.

records.title: Data-driven vestibular fMRI in PPPD and residual dizziness after BPPV: a narrative methodological review of AI-based phenotyping and longitudinal modeling.

content.title: Data-driven vestibular fMRI in PPPD and residual dizziness after BPPV: a narrative methodological review of AI-based phenotyping and longitudinal modeling.
content.abstract: Neuroimaging studies of vertigo and chronic dizziness have identified abnormalities across vestibular, visual, somatosensory, and cognitive-emotional networks, but conventional group-level analyses are limited in capturing individual heterogeneity and longitudinal change. This narrative methodological review integrates current evidence and proposes a framework combining functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced statistical modeling, anchored in two priority research scenarios: PPPD phenotyping and longitudinal characterization of residual dizziness after BPPV repositioning. AI, particularly unsupervised learning, may help identify candidate network subtypes from high-dimensional fMRI features, whereas mixed-effects, nonlinear, and latent trajectory models can evaluate their longitudinal stability, clinical relevance, and temporal evolution. Together, these approaches form a complementary pattern-discovery-longitudinal-validation framework. Current evidence, however, remains limited by small samples, single-center designs, technical heterogeneity, and scarce external validation. Accordingly, candidate PPPD subgroups and proposed recovery trajectories after BPPV repositioning should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than established fMRI phenotypes. The framework is therefore intended primarily as a research methodology for mechanistic investigation, candidate biomarker discovery, and prospective validation rather than as a clinically deployable decision tool. Future progress will require larger multicenter cohorts, harmonized acquisition and preprocessing, rigorous control of confounding and multiple testing, independent validation, and demonstration of incremental value beyond established clinical assessment.

records.title: Optimizing Treatment Strategies in the Bipolar Disorder Spectrum With Classical AI Approaches: Systematic Review of Performance, Bias, and Clinical Applicability.

content.title: Optimizing Treatment Strategies in the Bipolar Disorder Spectrum With Classical AI Approaches: Systematic Review of Performance, Bias, and Clinical Applicability.
content.abstract:
Background

Bipolar disorder (BD) is a complex and heterogeneous psychiatric condition, characterized by fluctuating clinical courses that affect approximately 1%-2% of the global population in their lifetime. Despite pharmacological advances, treatment response varies significantly among patients, making the identification of individualized treatment strategies a major challenge. Artificial Intelligence (AI), through its classical approaches, has emerged as a powerful tool in precision psychiatry to identify subtle patterns in complex data and inform personalized clinical decisions.

Objective

The present systematic review aimed to examine the current evidence on classical AI-supported treatment optimization in the BD spectrum.

Methods

The review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines. Four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase) were searched for original studies published after 2015 on the application of classical AI in the treatment of BD in adult patients. Publication bias was evaluated by visual inspection of a funnel plot. The methodological quality, risk of bias, and clinical applicability of the predictive models were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool for prediction models using regression or AI methods (PROBAST+AI; PROBAST+AI Working Group) tool.

Results

A total of 35 studies were included and classified into 5 outcome-based categories, including acute symptomatic response, long-term maintenance response, relapse and readmission risk, safety and dose optimization, and brain aging and phenotyping. Acute symptomatic response models performed modestly (pooled area under the curve [AUC] 0.68), while imaging improved accuracy (74%-77%). Long-term maintenance response models showed moderate-to-high performance (pooled AUC 0.80), with biomarker- and cellular-based models reaching 96%-99% accuracy. Relapse and readmission prediction achieved a pooled AUC of 0.71, with digital phenotyping and rule-based methods performing best (AUC 0.85-0.88). Safety and dose optimization models achieved 85%-97% accuracy. Brain aging and phenotyping studies highlighted accelerated brain aging in BD, partially mitigated by lithium, and revealed novel data-driven subgroups. However, 3 studies were considered at high risk of bias due to small sample sizes associated with disproportionately high-performance estimates. An additional study was identified as potentially biased because it lay markedly distant from the funnel plot's confidence line. Finally, the PROBAST+AI assessment revealed a high risk of bias in most studies, primarily due to data analysis limitations, small sample sizes, and lack of external validation.

Conclusions

The adoption of classical AI tools in BD serves as a driver for therapeutic optimization, although current AI tools in BD should still be considered exploratory rather than ready for clinical use. Effective implementation in real-world clinical scenarios requires more robust, transparent, and externally validated models to ensure reliability and generalizability.

records.title: Pan-immune-inflammation value for risk stratification of adverse cardiovascular outcomes in acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Pan-immune-inflammation value for risk stratification of adverse cardiovascular outcomes in acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain at residual cardiovascular risk. The pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), integrating neutrophil, platelet, monocyte, and lymphocyte counts, has been proposed as a candidate prognostic biomarker in this population, but the evidence has not been formally synthesised. We evaluated the prognostic and discriminatory value of PIV in adults with ACS undergoing PCI.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and CNKI were searched from inception, supplemented by trial registries, Google Scholar, and reference hand-searching. Cohort studies reporting associations between PIV and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; primary outcome), all-cause mortality, cardiovascular or cardiac mortality, angiographic no-reflow or slow-flow, or post-contrast renal injury were eligible. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and QUIPS risk-of-bias assessment. Adjusted hazard ratios, odds ratios, and AUC values were pooled separately using random-effects models; certainty was rated with GRADE. PROSPERO: CRD420261378751.

Results

Nineteen cohort studies (n = 18,715) were included. Higher PIV was associated with study-defined MACE (adjusted HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.20-2.27; k = 2; I² = 0.0%; low certainty) and all-cause mortality (HR 3.51, 95% CI 2.15-5.74; k = 2; I² = 0.0%; moderate certainty). A single study reported an association with cardiac mortality (HR 3.24, 95% CI 1.34-7.81; low certainty). PIV showed consistent discrimination for no-reflow or slow-flow (AUC 0.828, 95% CI 0.808-0.846; k = 2; I² = 0.0%; moderate certainty) and heterogeneous discrimination for post-contrast renal injury (AUC 0.771, 95% CI 0.617-0.875; k = 5; I² = 95.1%; very low certainty). Risk of bias was moderate in 16 studies and high in three.

Conclusion

Elevated PIV may be associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes in ACS patients undergoing PCI, particularly long-term all-cause mortality and angiographic no-reflow or slow-flow. However, evidence is limited by observational designs, small numbers of studies for several outcomes, heterogeneous cut-offs, and risk-of-bias concerns. PIV should be regarded as a promising supplementary marker requiring prospective multicentre validation, comparison with established inflammatory indices, and assessment of incremental value beyond GRACE or TIMI before routine clinical use.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261378751.

records.title: Translational Applications of Retinal Biomarkers in Chronic Cardiovascular, Neurological, Metabolic, and Renal Diseases.

content.title: Translational Applications of Retinal Biomarkers in Chronic Cardiovascular, Neurological, Metabolic, and Renal Diseases.
content.abstract: Imaging the retina is a powerful non-invasive probe of systemic vascular, neurological, metabolic, and renal disease, making it a cornerstone of the new field of systemic oculomics. Advanced retinal imaging techniques like optical coherence tomography (OCT) and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) provide detailed imaging of structural and microvascular changes potentially associated with systemic disease. Derived from fundus photography, structural imaging, vascular imaging, and artificial intelligence-based image analysis, retinal biomarkers have been associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, neurodegenerative disorders, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and related clinical outcomes. However, the translational maturity of these biomarkers is variable depending on imaging modality, target disease, intended clinical use, and level of validation. Longitudinally, retinal vascular characteristics have been associated with cardiovascular as well as cerebrovascular outcomes. In addition, optical coherence tomography has provided reproducible measures of neuroaxonal injury in selected neurological conditions. This is especially true for multiple sclerosis. The majority of retinal biomarkers in Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, chronic kidney disease, and systemic risk prediction remain experimental because of heterogeneous methodologies, insufficient external validation, and insufficient evidence for incremental clinical utility. Diabetes is the most developed translational model with established retinal screening pathways and validated ocular applications of imaging and artificial intelligence, although these cannot be directly extrapolated to systemic diagnosis or treatment guidance. This narrative review assesses retinal biomarkers for cardiovascular, neurological, metabolic, and renal disease with a focus on analytical validity, clinical validity, incremental value, clinical utility, and implementation. The retina is increasingly accepted as a site for discovery of systemic biomarkers and adjunctive risk assessment, although most applications to systemic disease remain to be standardized, validated independently, and studied prospectively before being suitable for routine clinical use.

records.title: Privacy, Security & Governance Frameworks for AI-Powered Wearable Internet of Health Things in Elderly Care: A Comprehensive Review.

content.title: Privacy, Security & Governance Frameworks for AI-Powered Wearable Internet of Health Things in Elderly Care: A Comprehensive Review.
content.abstract: The global aging population is expanding at an unprecedented rate, with projections indicating that 1.4 billion people will be aged 60 years or older by 2030 and 2.1 billion by 2050, placing immense pressure on healthcare systems worldwide. Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered wearable Internet of Health Things (IoHT) devices - including smartwatches, biosensors, and continuous health monitors - have emerged as transformative tools for real-time elderly health monitoring, fall detection, and predictive analytics. However, the massive collection of sensitive biometric data by these devices raises critical concerns regarding privacy, security, and governance that remain insufficiently addressed, particularly for elderly populations. This comprehensive review synthesizes evidence from 333 peer-reviewed articles published between 2018 and 2025 cross PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar to identify, analyze, and compare governance frameworks for AI-powered wearable IoHT in elderly care. The analysis reveals significant regulatory fragmentation across jurisdictions: while the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and AI Act provide the most comprehensive rights-based framework, the United States relies on a patchwork of sector-specific regulations with notable gaps for consumer wearables, and Asia-Pacific nations exhibit highly variable approaches ranging from mature (Singapore, Japan) to nascent (Indonesia, Malaysia). Elderly-specific provisions remain conspicuously absent across all regulatory regimes examined. This review proposes a novel five-layer integrative governance framework - the first to unify technical security, privacy protection, ethical AI governance, regulatory compliance, and person-centered governance specifically designed for elderly care contexts. The framework addresses unique vulnerabilities associated with cognitive decline, reduced digital literacy, and caregiver dependency. Findings underscore the urgent need for harmonized, age-sensitive regulatory approaches and privacy-preserving technologies such as federated learning and differential privacy to ensure that AI-powered wearable IoHT fulfills its promise of enhancing elderly healthcare without compromising dignity, autonomy, or data security.

records.title: What are the beneficial treatment strategies in maintaining T lymphocyte subsets after cancer surgery? A systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: What are the beneficial treatment strategies in maintaining T lymphocyte subsets after cancer surgery? A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Perioperative alterations in T lymphocyte subsets significantly impact tumor recurrence and postoperative recovery; therefore, identifying optimal strategies to maintain these immune parameters is essential for improving cancer surgery outcomes. The immunomodulatory effects of different tumor therapies, especially those on key T cell subsets, still lack systematic comparisons.

Objective
